articles.title: How AI Is Changing the Pace of Discovery for Millions Living With Dementia
articles.summary:
There are 57 million people worldwide living with dementia today. For the researchers working to help them, the obstacle isn’t a lack of effort — it’s too much data, too few experts to synthesize it and a pace of discovery that can’t keep up with the disease.
The Consortium for Biomedical Research and AI in Neurodegeneration (C-BRAIN), working with NVIDIA, is using AI to change that.
Alzheimer’s disease is one of today’s leading global health challenges, with over 10 million new dementia cases diagnosed each year. Despite a 7x increase in National Institutes of Health funding in the last 15 years — reaching $3.9 billion annually — no treatment has been found to stop, prevent or reverse the disease yet.
The bottlenecks are not enough high impact scientific findings, too much data living in institutional silos and too slow a pace of synthesis to keep up with the research that is published.
C-BRAIN, led by Dr. Randall Bateman and a consortium of 18 member institutions across academic, philanthropic, pharma and research organizations, launched in November 2025 to help scientists make better, faster discoveries by accelerating the research that makes new treatments possible.
“We have a window of opportunity with artificial intelligence to do research fundamentally different than we’ve ever done before, in a way that accelerates discoveries to help patients,” said Bateman, founder and director of C-BRAIN and the Charles F. and Joanne Knight Distinguished Professor of Neurology at t…

articles.title: Smart Window adds new form filling and page watching features | The Mozilla Blog
articles.summary:
Skip the busywork with Smart Window
The days might be getting shorter, but your to-do list is only getting longer. Whether you’re getting a head start on holiday shopping or planning your next career move, Smart Window’s newest features will help you keep up.
Firefox’s opt-in AI browsing experience can now use information from tabs you choose to help fill out forms. It can also watch web pages and notify you about specific changes you’ve asked it to track.
Let your open tabs fill in the blanks
Job applications ask for your work history; event registrations ask for a professional bio. If those details are already in your open tabs, Smart Window can now use pages you choose to suggest what to enter, saving you extra clicks and some Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V.
For example, Smart Window could use information from your online portfolio or professional profile to fill in your work history, or draw on those details to draft an answer to a question like “Tell me about a time when…” Firefox’s regular autofill still handles saved information such as your name and address, which can be entered directly into forms without relying on AI models.
To get started, click into a form field. If the form has at least four text fields that Smart Window can help fill, you’ll see “Fill from sources” appear in the dropdown, along with a recommended source page. articles.title: Cybersecurity Issue Forces a Major New Mexico Hospital to Divert Patients and Close Clinics
articles.summary:
A major hospital network in New Mexico raced to fix a cybersecurity issue on Monday that forced it to send ambulances to other hospitals and left the state without an emergency department capable of treating the most serious injuries.
The University of New Mexico Health System told people not to show up at its main hospital in Albuquerque and canceled appointments at its more than 30 clinics. It said it was working to resolve the issue, the extent and nature of which was not immediately clear.
The hospital network conducts about 900,000 outpatient visits and receives 100,000 emergency room visits each year, according to its website. It operates the state’s only Level 1 trauma center.
Presbyterian Healthcare Services and Lovelace Health System, two other major healthcare providers in New Mexico, said they were coordinating with the UNM Health System, including taking additional patients.
The UNM Health System said in a statement that its hospitals and clinics began resuming operations in phases later in the day.
Multiple UNM Health System employees said they heard messages across their computers while working late Monday morning that claimed to have stolen student and employee data and patient information.
A spokesperson for the health system wouldn’t comment, saying that the incident remains an active law enforcement investigation. FBI spokesperson Margot Cravens in Albuquerque said the agency was “assisting our partner” but declined further comment.

articles.summary:
En Allemagne, la police autoroutière de Hohenbrunn, en Haute-Bavière, a arrêté un Tesla Cybertruck sur l’A99, près de Vaterstetten, dans la nuit du samedi 24 au dimanche 25 octobre 2026, rapporte le quotidien régional Merkur.
Derrière le volant, un conducteur suédois âgé de 50 ans qui n’avait qu’un simple permis B (celui pour voitures type « M1 »), autorisant la conduite de véhicule de 3,5 tonnes maximum. Or, le pick-up électrique de Tesla est bien loin du seuil autorisé puisqu’il revendique un poids total en charge (PTAC) de 4,2 tonnes.
Les policiers lui ont interdit de reprendre la route et ont garé le véhicule, immatriculé en Pologne, devant leur poste, en attendant qu’un conducteur titulaire du bon permis vienne le récupérer.
Trop lourd pour le permis B et pas homologué
Selon Tesla, le Cybertruck pèse entre 2 775 kg et 3 129 kg à vide, selon les versions et les pneumatique. Jusqu’ici, sous la barre des fameux 3,5 tonnes. Sauf que le permis B se calcule sur le PTAC, la masse maximale autorisée, passagers et chargement compris et toutes les versions du pick-up dépassent ce seuil. En Europe, il est donc nécessaire d’être titulaire d’un permis C1, celui des petits camions allant jusqu’à 7,5 tonnes.

articles.title: 3 Ways to Boost MoE Inference on NVIDIA DGX Spark | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.summary:
Generating tokens faster starts with identifying what limits inference performance. In the batch-size-1 evaluation of Ling-3.0-flash from Inclusion AI on NVIDIA DGX Spark, profiling showed that decoding was memory-bound: reading model weights drove execution time. Two operations stood out—the mixture-of-experts (MoE) computation and the output-layer projection that produces scores across the model’s vocabulary.
Those findings pointed to two ways to improve performance: reduce the weight traffic in each decode step and generate more tokens per verification round. This post examines three techniques that address those costs:
- Humming MXFP4 MoE kernels to improve execution of the routed-expert computation.
- Online FP8 quantization of the output layer, or LM head, to reduce its weight-read volume.
- Multi-token prediction (MTP) speculative decoding with NEXTN to draft and verify multiple tokens together.
This post explains how each optimization works, measures its effect, and examines an integration issue that can make the combined configuration slower than the baseline. Ling-3.0-flash serves as the implementation example, with code and deployment instructions in the Ling cookbook.
Model and baseline configuration
The evaluation used Ling-3.0-flash-fp4, a mixture-of-experts model with 124 billion total parameters and 5.1 billion active parameters per token. The model has 42 layers: 35 Kimi Delta Attention (KDA) linear-attention layers and seven multi-head latent attention (MLA)…

articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
Exowatt beats frontier models on accuracy with SageMaker serverless model customization
Exowatt builds modular, dispatchable solar systems that deliver reliable power for energy-intensive applications such as AI data centers. Its flagship product, the Exowatt P3, captures solar energy through optical lenses, stores it as heat in a long-duration thermal battery, and dispatches electricity on demand through a heat engine. Unlike grid-tied photovoltaic solar systems, P3 powers data centers directly behind the meter, helping data centers come online without waiting in multi-year grid interconnection queues. Exowatt builds a fleet of AI agents that monitor and triage live alarms and support operational decisions for solar systems, often at the edge, with limited or no connectivity. As its fleet scales from test benches toward manufacturing and thousands of deployed field units, the intelligence layer that operates these systems must scale with it.
In this post, we show how Exowatt used Amazon SageMaker AI serverless model customization to build a repeatable AI pipeline. The pipeline produces task-specific fine-tuned models for two deployment targets, edge and cloud, achieving higher accuracy than frontier models at up to 49× lower cost.

articles.title: Entenda a origem da Lua do Caçador que brilhou no céu este mês
articles.summary:
A Lua do Caçador iluminou o céu de diferentes países durante o último fim de semana. No Brasil, o fenômeno também pôde ser observado nas regiões onde as condições do tempo permitiram.
A Lua cheia atingiu seu ponto máximo à 1h12 de segunda-feira (26), pelo horário de Brasília, segundo a NASA, agência espacial norte-americana. O nome tem origem em antigas tradições de caça do Hemisfério Norte.
A origem do nome e a observação no Brasil
A Lua do Caçador não é um fenômeno astronômico diferente de uma Lua cheia comum. A denominação surgiu de costumes do Hemisfério Norte, onde outubro marca o outono.
Após as colheitas, os campos ficavam mais abertos, e a luz da Lua ajudava os caçadores a localizar animais e obter alimentos para armazenar durante o inverno.
A tradição também está relacionada ao horário em que a Lua nasce nessa época do ano. Durante várias noites consecutivas, ela pode surgir em horários próximos, prolongando a claridade natural depois do pôr do sol.
Esse comportamento ajuda a explicar a associação histórica entre a Lua cheia de outubro e as atividades de caça. Entre os aspectos que caracterizam essa tradição estão:
- Calendário sazonal: a denominação está associada ao outono no Hemisfério Norte.
- Costumes antigos: a luz lunar auxiliava atividades realizadas após as colheitas.
- Preparação para o inverno: a caça ajudava a obter alimentos para os meses mais frios.
- Visibilidade noturna: o nascimento da Lua em horários próximos favorecia a iluminação após o pôr do sol…

articles.title: I Tried to Fool a Scientific Publisher With AI
articles.summary:
I Used AI to Fake a Scientific Paper. Here’s What Happened
My experiment with an IEEE journal revealed AI’s threats to scholarly publishing
Science has a spam problem. And the spam filter is getting clogged up.
According to all reports, academic publishing is drowning in what has come to be called AI slop: low-quality, mass-produced content generated with AI. By 2025, an estimated 57 percent of all published academic articles exhibited detectable evidence of large language model (LLM) influence, a massive jump from 12 percent in 2023. What’s more, over 12 percent of Nature Communications reviews were found to be completely AI-generated in 2025.
Given that for every 40 papers showing statistical evidence of AI usage in 2025, only one formally disclosed it, these figures likely grossly underestimate LLM involvement today. Of course, evidence of AI use doesn’t necessarily mean a paper is slop. But some estimates suggest that hundreds of thousands of fake, often AI-generated, publications are now produced annually.
“It’s not just the [scientific] record under threat, it’s science as a whole,” warns Amanda Sulicz, IEEE’s research-integrity manager. “AI slop is completely eroding trust in science and every scientific process that we’ve worked for centuries to create.”
Yet statistics and statements claiming that the problem is big—perhaps even existential for science—don’t really get the message across. Just how easy is it to use AI to create a convincing but completely fake paper? …

articles.title: Windows 11 ajoute un bouton pour réactiver votre abonnement Microsoft 365, mais rien pour le résilier — Frandroid
articles.summary:
Microsoft a trouvé une nouvelle place dans Windows 11 pour Microsoft 365, son abonnement qui donne accès à Word, Excel et au stockage en ligne OneDrive. Dans les notes de version publiées le 23 octobre pour les testeurs de son programme Windows Insider, l’éditeur explique que les abonnés qui ont désactivé le renouvellement automatique pourront le réactiver directement dans les Paramètres, sans passer par une page web. Le bouton apparaît sur la page d’accueil des Paramètres, sur la page Comptes et dans le menu Démarrer. Autrement dit, ceux qui avaient choisi de ne plus être prélevés de 99 euros par an pour la formule Personnel retrouveront l’option dans le menu qu’ils ouvrent le plus souvent.
Sean Endicott, de Windows Central, n’hésite pas à comparer Windows 11 à un jeu free-to-play, ces jeux gratuits qui se rentabilisent en poussant sans cesse le joueur à payer. Pour lui, tout ce qui incite à acheter un produit ou un service est une publicité, quelle que soit l’étiquette qu’on lui colle. Microsoft présente au contraire le bouton comme une simplification, qui évite d’ouvrir un navigateur pour gérer son abonnement.

Windows 11 : nouveautés, configuration requise, installation, téléchargement, tout savoir sur le système de Microsoft
            
Un bouton pour réactiver, rien pour résilier
Les notes de version de Microsoft ne parlent que de rallumer la facturation récurrente. Rien n’indique que Windows 11 permettra de la couper au même endroit. Pour arrêt…

articles.title: Le Danemark abandonne en silence son test d’un Office open source, sans même en tirer le bilan
articles.summary:
Le ministère danois de la Numérisation a mis fin à son expérimentation d’une alternative open source à Microsoft Office, révèle Computerworld le 20 octobre. Le projet, lancé à l’été 2025 avec 38 agents, ne sera pas repris et n’a fait l’objet d’aucun bilan. Entre-temps, ce ministère a disparu : il a été fusionné en juin avec celui de l’Enseignement supérieur et de la Recherche.
À l’époque, la ministre de la Numérisation, Caroline Stage, présentait ce test comme un pas vers l’indépendance technologique vis-à-vis des États-Unis, et saluait un « pas bienvenu dans la bonne direction ». Le ministère espérait se passer d’Office 365 avant la fin de l’automne 2025.
Les agents testaient Collabora, une suite bureautique britannique basée sur LibreOffice, fournie par le Danois cBrain et reliée à F2, son système de gestion de dossiers. Le test visait notamment à vérifier l’échange de documents entre les formats de Microsoft et les formats ouverts.
Un test arrêté avant d’être évalué
L’expérience aurait pris fin au moment où la Première ministre a convoqué des élections anticipées, fin février 2026. Un porte-parole du ministère aurait confirmé qu’aucune reprise n’est envisagée.
Des agents auraient buté sur la mise en forme des documents, des pages blanches inexpliquées et le suivi des modifications. Rien ne dit si ces difficultés ont été résolues, ni si elles ont pesé dans la décision d’arrêter.

articles.title: Fine-Tuning NVIDIA Nemotron to Know Local Rules, Not Just Local Languages | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.summary:
As AI adoption expands globally, people across languages and cultures are using it in more aspects of their daily lives. General-purpose language models serve as a powerful foundation, but they sometimes lack the local knowledge, cultural nuance, and precision a particular application needs.
Post-training can adapt an open model to these needs. With suitable data and evaluation, it can improve accuracy and usefulness while supporting safer interactions with the model. This gives countries and industries greater control over how their agents reflect local priorities and serve the people who use them.
NVIDIA built Nemotron-Personas-France with French AI startup Pleias, and Nemotron-Personas-Belgium with Pleias and Belgian university KU Leuven. Both are part of the open NVIDIA Nemotron data program, which includes locale-grounded persona datasets for 12 countries that developers can use to adapt open models market by market.
In this blog, we will discuss how to take Nemotron open models and post-train them with Nemotron datasets to tailor them for regional languages and cultures.
The difference post-training makes
Let’s say you are developing an agent for the passport agency in France and the agent gets a customer question like this:
Je ne peux plus me déplacer à cause de ma santé. Comment faire ma demande de passeport?
(Translation: I can no longer travel because of my health. How do I apply for my passport?)

articles.title: Sur World of Warcraft Forever, vous pouvez réserver votre pseudo, mais il faut payer
articles.summary:
Envie de vous faire un nom sur World of Warcraft ? Avec WoW Forever, c’est possible sans réaliser le moindre exploit en jeu : cette troisième version du célèbre MMORPG de Blizzard introduit un second nom, que Blizzard compare lui-même à un nom de famille. Une première pour WoW. Pour celles et ceux qui craignent de ne pas obtenir l’identité de leur rêve, Blizzard ouvre une réservation anticipée des noms, à condition de passer à la caisse.
À partir de ce mardi 27 octobre, à 18 heures (heure de Paris), la réservation anticipée des noms de personnages pour World of Warcraft Forever ouvre, et cela jusqu’au 3 novembre. Les joueurs et joueuses qui tiennent à leur pseudo peuvent donc le réclamer plus d’une semaine avant la sortie du jeu, fixée au jeudi 5 novembre à minuit (heure de Paris).
Premier arrivé, premier servi, et il faut payer
Il y a cependant trois limites à connaître. D’abord, Blizzard gère les demandes sur la base du premier arrivé, premier servi. Rien ne garantit donc d’obtenir la combinaison prénom + nom de son choix. Dans WoW Forever, il n’y a plus vraiment de serveur : chaque nom complet doit être unique dans toute la région (l’Europe, pour les joueurs français), et plus seulement sur un royaume.
Ensuite, cette réservation est… payante. Elle est réservée aux joueurs qui ont préacheté l’un des trois packs payants : le pack héroïque des Éolides, le pack épique des Éolides ou la Warcraft Forever Collection. Ils coûtent respectivement 29,99, 59,99 et 79,99 euros, et chaq…

articles.title: Fix evaluation bias to unlock better models on Amazon Bedrock | Amazon Web Services
articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
Fix evaluation bias to unlock better models on Amazon Bedrock
This post was co-authored with Khaled Thabit, Meriem Boughrara, and Mohamed Desouky from Property Finder.
The engineering team at Property Finder, a digital real estate application, discovered that 96.8 percent of their evaluation labels had been inherited directly from a single model’s predictions rather than verified by human experts. Their ground truth was systematically skewed toward the incumbent model, making every alternative appear to underperform. The labels also had errors, but the bias was what blocked objective model comparison. They uncovered this when migrating their vision AI workload to a more cost-effective option on Amazon Bedrock.
Property Finder processes tens of thousands of property images every day across the Middle East and North Africa (MENA). Their system evaluates 11 quality attributes per image. These cover watermark detection, room classification, furnishing status, photo quality, and construction indicators. That’s thousands of new property listings with an average of 15 images each. All need quality assessment before going live.
Property Finder needed a more cost-effective option. But measured against those labels, any alternative was at a disadvantage.
The hardest part was not finding a better model. It was discovering that their evaluation methodology itself was the blocker.

articles.title: Google’s next Genie AI model generates more realistic experiences
articles.summary:
Google announced today its Genie 4 world model for generating interactive experiences using AI. The company says the model has four main updates: It allows for more realistic worlds, lets users update an experience in real time with a natural language prompt, can generate audio, and uses Gemini 3.8 Flash under the hood to help with its simulations. It also can create experiences that are about two minutes long, up from one minute for the previous Genie 3 model.
Google’s next Genie AI model generates more realistic experiences
The Genie 4 world model offers more realism and can create audio to accompany its interactive worlds.
Google is pitching Genie 4 as a tool that could be helpful for things like pre-visualization for filmmakers, prototyping game ideas, and making training scenarios for robots. But the company warns that, as simulations run longer, details and object permanence can shift over time.
I haven’t been able to try Genie 4 for myself — it’s launching first as a “research preview” to “trusted testers” — so I can’t tell you how it compares to the Genie 3-powered Project Genie, which I used to generate bad Nintendo knockoffs. But here are some examples from Google demonstrating what’s possible with the new model.
Genie 4 will be “coming soon” to Google AI Ultra subscribers, Google says, and the company has opened a waitlist where you can apply to be able to try it in Project Genie.

articles.title: Announcing SOCI-indexed images for faster SageMaker AI jobs | Amazon Web Services
articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
Announcing SOCI-indexed images for faster SageMaker AI jobs
Every minute your deep learning container image spends downloading is a minute you pay for and a minute your team waits. Container image download is pure overhead: billable job time that produces no model progress. For modern deep learning images, that overhead is several minutes on every single job. Today, we’re excited to announce Seekable OCI (SOCI) indexing for Amazon SageMaker AI Training and Amazon SageMaker AI processing jobs, which takes full container image download off the critical path of every job.
With SOCI indexing, SageMaker AI lazy-loads your container image. It fetches only the files needed to start the container and streams the rest in the background as your code runs, so your job begins in seconds instead of minutes. You adopt it by pointing to a pre-indexed AWS Deep Learning Container (DLC) or adding an index to your own image. Neither approach requires changes to your job definition, entry point, or data channels. The result is faster job starts, lower job cost, and more time spent building models rather than waiting on infrastructure.
SOCI-indexed images start Amazon SageMaker AI training containers in seconds, with no impact on training performance. As we show in the What we measured section, this reduced GPU idle time during image pulls by up to 90 percent in our benchmarks.

articles.title: What Took the Internet Offline in Q3 2026
articles.summary:
What took the Internet offline in Q3 2026
The Internet can feel invisible when everything is working normally. But when connectivity breaks, the many systems it depends upon become evident in an instant. Because Cloudflare’s global network handles more than 20% of the web’s traffic, it offers a unique perspective of how Internet traffic is behaving. When failures in infrastructure, power, policy, or security disrupt access to the Internet, Cloudflare Radar can observe the impact by monitoring traffic to our customers. Each quarter, we review the disruptions detected and annotated on Radar, highlighting what happened, where it happened, and the broader conditions that shaped each event.
In this post, we examine the major categories of Internet disruptions observed during the third quarter of 2026, including government-directed shutdowns, power outages and natural disasters.
Disruptions at a glance
Between July and September, Internet disruptions were largely driven by failures in the systems the Internet depends on. Power grids failed in Cuba, Honduras, Guam, Ukraine, and several other countries. Natural disasters damaged electricity and telecommunications infrastructure from Nepal to Colombia. articles.title: Dead Popcorn Time Updater Put Millions of Computers at Risk of Takeover
articles.summary:
Eye Security researchers have disabled the update mechanism of an abandoned Popcorn Time fork and sinkholed its domains.
A BitTorrent client that allowed users to view movies downloaded from the web, Popcorn Time was highly popular over a decade ago, but the project was abandoned in 2014. A legal alternative has been in the works since early 2025.
The vulnerable update mechanism targeted by Eye Security belongs to Time4Popcorn, a fork of the original that has been distributed under the name Popcorn Time.
Eye Security discovered that the abandoned updater is connecting to its remote servers over HTTP to request updates, and that many of the update domains have been abandoned, while others are owned by third parties and parked.
The updater runs in the background at system boot, does not feature code signing, and downloads and runs any executable its domain supplies.
After registering the abandoned domain popcorntimeupd.xyz, Eye Security observed millions of systems connecting to it. Systems also connected to other domains, and the company registered some of those as well.
Most of the identified systems were Windows (2.5-3 million), with the remaining running macOS (250,000-350,000) and Android (less than 200,000).

Scientists recreate a bizarre quantum effect that stops a particle cold
- Date:
- October 13, 2026
- Source:
- University of Oxford
- Summary:
- Oxford physicists have recreated a bizarre quantum effect in which a particle responds to a magnetic field without ever traveling through it. Using a hybrid quantum computer, they demonstrated how introducing a simulated magnetic flux could completely halt a particle's movement through quantum interference. The experiment brings a decades-old prediction into a new setting where matter and quantum fields influence one another.
- Share:
A particle does not have to pass through a magnetic field to be influenced by it. That surprising feature of quantum physics has now been recreated by researchers at the University of Oxford, who used a hybrid quantum computer to demonstrate how an invisible magnetic influence can bring a simulated particle's movement to a complete stop.
The experiment reproduced a phenomenon known as the Aharonov-Bohm effect, in which a charged particle traveling around a region containing magnetic flux experiences a measurable change in its quantum state, even though its path never takes it through the magnetic field itself.
The Oxford team achieved this using a quantum system that combines qubits, the basic units of quantum information, with quantum oscillators, which represent vibrating motion. articles.title: En 2015, Jay-Z compró Tidal por 56 millones de dólares. Seis años después, Square, la empresa de Jack Dorsey, acordó pagar 297 millones por su control
articles.summary:
Jay-Z pasó de comprar el negocio de Tidal a vender su control en él a Square en el espacio de seis años. El acuerdo de compra de 2015 fue de unos 56 millones de dólares, y el de 2021, 297 millones. La historia tiene una peculiaridad que debe recordarse: la suma difiere debido a que se trata de acuerdos distintos y, en consecuencia, es imposible determinar el beneficio individual del rapero solo con esas cifras.
El primer paso hacia ello ocurrió el 30 de enero de 2015, cuando Project Panther Bidco, la empresa controlada por Jay-Z, presentó una oferta por todas las acciones de la empresa sueca Aspiro, madre de Tidal y WiMP. Con un valor de oferta estimado de 464 millones de coronas suecas, la firma se evaluó en torno a los 56 millones de dólares al cambio del día, aproximadamente 49,5 millones de euros en ese momento.
La adquisición se completó en marzo. Sus condiciones se dieron por cumplidas el 13 del mes, y el 30, Jay-Z presentó su servicio con la participación de otras superestrellas. Este incluía a Beyoncé, Alicia Keys, Rihanna, Madonna, Usher, Nicki Minaj, Chris Martin y otros. Este fue el resultado del paso previo, que se convirtió en una ventaja para todos: los músicos tuvieron la oportunidad de poseer una parte de la plataforma con audio de alta calidad y contenidos exclusivos.

Sa grande promesse est sa plage dynamique, c’est-à-dire sa capacité à capturer en même temps les zones très claires et très sombres d’une scène. articles.title: How a Fake Signal Could Fool Every Robot Safeguard
articles.summary:
This article is brought to you by VicOne.
A mobile robot slows for someone in a hallway. A collaborative arm eases its movement as a worker approaches. A humanoid pauses to let a person pass. Each response depends on information about the robot or its surroundings: a distance reading, a position estimate, or a stop signal.
But what happens when one of those inputs is wrong, and the robot still responds exactly as designed? The mobile robot reads the hallway as clear while someone is still there. The arm estimates that the worker is farther away. The humanoid does not receive a stop signal as a person crosses its path.
In each case, a fault could cause that mismatch. So could deliberate manipulation.
At VicOne LAB R7, we examine how manipulated inputs can change robot behavior — and what that means for the systems meant to keep people safe.
How an untrusted input can change a robot’s behavior
A robot does more than measure its surroundings. It may interpret what it sees and hears to decide what to do next. Information placed in its environment can therefore influence its actions.
Published research shows how this can happen. In a study of vision-language-action (VLA) models, a patch in a camera’s view reduced task success in simulated robot tests. FreezeVLA found that an adversarial image could cause tested models to ignore later instructions. Although the studies used different methods, both demonstrate how visual input can interfere with a robot’s intended task.

articles.title: En attendant le premier Mac tactile, Apple met à jour les MacBook Pro et iMac avec la puce M6
articles.summary:
Les rumeurs ont vu juste : Apple prévoit bien une semaine d’annonces. Après les iPhone 18 Pro et l’iPhone Duo, les Apple Watch, les AirPods 5, le HomeView, l’Apple TV et le HomePod mini, puis l’iPad mini avec un écran OLED annoncé la veille, la marque poursuit son automne fou avec de petites révisions des MacBook Pro et iMac dévoilées le 27 octobre par communiqué de presse.
Il n’y a pas d’écran OLED ou de nouveau design ici : la grande nouveauté est l’arrivée de la puce M6, déjà aperçue avec le Mac mini fin août.

Seul le MacBook Pro le moins cher est mis à jour : les versions « Pro » et « Max » attendront sans doute mercredi.
Le MacBook Pro 14 pouces d’entrée de gamme conserve le même design que les anciennes générations, mais remplace la puce M5 par la M6. L’ordinateur utilise toujours un mini-LED 120 Hz (jusqu’à 1 600 nits en HDR, avec une option nano-texture) : Apple ne change quasiment rien dans ce qui ressemble à une dernière itération de ce design (l’année prochaine, on peut imaginer que tous les nouveaux MacBook Pro auront le nouveau design tactile). La connectique reste identique (HDMI, MagSafe 3, trois ports Thunderbolt 4, lecteur SDXC et prise jack), tout comme les deux coloris, noir sidéral et argent. articles.title: L'iPhone Duo soumis à un test de résistance : l'appareil montre ses limites, Apple réagit
articles.summary:
Nous vous en parlions récemment, iFixit, une entreprise américaine spécialisée dans la réparation d’appareils électroniques, a passé au peigne fin l’iPhone Duo. Après d’innombrables tests, l’entreprise en est arrivée à deux conclusions : l’appareil présente une bonne réparabilité, mais aussi, et surtout, « un énorme problème d’écran ». iFixit a ainsi repéré une fragilité notable au niveau de l’écran interne du smartphone, sans parvenir à définir avec précision la cause, même si plusieurs hypothèses sont avancées. Zack, de la chaîne YouTube JerryRigEverything, a quant à lui réalisé son propre test de résistance de l’iPhone Duo. Son constat est sans appel : le premier smartphone pliant d’Apple a échoué à l’épreuve. Face à la multiplication d’utilisateurs faisant état d’une faiblesse au niveau de l’écran, Apple a réagi.
Du sable, une flamme et un test de flexibilité
Autant le dire tout de suite, les méthodes mobilisées par Zack pour tester la résistance des nouveaux smartphones sont radicales. L’objectif est justement de pousser un appareil qui vient de sortir dans ses retranchements. Comme nous pouvons le voir à partir de la dixième minute de la vidéo ci-dessous, le youtubeur a tout d’abord aspergé (pour ne pas dire inonder) un iPhone Duo de sable. Mauvaise nouvelle : des grains de sable se sont retrouvés dans la charnière du téléphone, réduisant ainsi fortement sa capacité à se fermer et à s’ouvrir avec fluidité. articles.title: The imec Report: Scaling Optical Interconnects For The AI Era
articles.summary:
Unprecedented demand for bandwidth calls for bringing optics closer to silicon through a fundamental rethinking of the optical interconnect roadmap.
The explosive growth of cloud computing and AI – from generative, and reasoning, to (ultimately) agentic systems – is creating unprecedented demand for bandwidth, as the amount of data that must be moved both within and between data centers continues to surge. In turn, this exposes growing limitations in the underlying interconnects that not only span the data center fabric and rack level but also extend deep inside servers – down to where they link XPUs, memory, and other system components at the package and die level.
Copper-based (electrical) interconnects have long been the industry’s workhorse thanks to their low cost, simplicity, and reliability. Yet today, they are increasingly hitting fundamental limits: while highly energy-efficient electrical links can be realized, they are typically confined to very short reaches (on the order of millimeters). At longer distances and higher lane rates, power consumption rises sharply, thermal constraints intensify, and signal integrity degrades. In other words, electrical I/O is rapidly becoming a key barrier to scaling next-generation AI and machine learning systems.
Optical interconnects have emerged as a critical path forward. By transmitting data using light rather than electrical signals, they are far less sensitive to distance, enabling much better energy efficiency while mitigat…

Long before Dominion Dynamics closed its $139-million Series A round this summer, it faced a more basic financial problem.
The Ottawa-based startup was growing fast and quickly becoming a major player in Canadian defence technology. But its legacy bank was holding it back. That’s when a friend pointed Carkner to Venn, the Toronto-based FinTech that lets businesses move money, manage team spending, and sync transactions with their accounting software—all from one platform.

articles.title: La UE abre la vía para multar a Google Maps por representar a Ceuta y Melilla como “territorios en disputa” con Marruecos
articles.summary:
Google Maps traza una línea gris discontinua en las fronteras terrestres de Ceuta y Melilla con Marruecos. Una queja ha pedido a la Comisión Europea que actúe para que Google Maps cambie el trazado de acuerdo con el Reglamento de Servicios Digitales.
La nota del Partido Popular sobre este asunto apareció hace poco: un comunicado sobre ambas ciudades, según el cual los coordinadores de la Comisión de Peticiones habían aprobado la iniciativa. Quien interpone la queja considera ambigua la representación de las fronteras y dice que Google debería mostrar una línea continua, no una línea discontinua. Pide a la Comisión Europea que actúe en relación con los riesgos de desinformación que, según la queja, podría generar el mapa. Su queja refleja su posición y no demuestra que se haya incumplido el reglamento.
El Observatorio de Ceuta y Melilla ha informado de que su director, Carlos Echeverría, había escrito a Google España en 2023 sobre el tema. También apareció en una nota del Observatorio el 23 de septiembre de 2026, que afirmaba que el asunto aún no se había resuelto.
Las notas de Google indican que el servicio diferencia entre varias fronteras. En el apartado sobre fronteras y nombres de los países, las líneas grises continuas se reservan a las fronteras internacionales sin discusión, y las discontinuas, a aquellas cuya definición sea objeto de controversia (y a determinados límites provisionales o decididos por tratados). articles.title: Volkswagen peut-il importer en Europe ses voitures électriques chinoises à 20 000 € ?
articles.summary:
Beaucoup de marques n’hésitent pas à se plier en quatre pour séduire le marché chinois. Il faut dire que cet ancien eldorado de l’automobile a toujours fait rêver nombre de constructeurs qui ont investi des sommes colossales pour réussir leur entrée. Cela passe par la création de modèles spécifiquement taillés pour la clientèle locale, une stratégie longtemps adoptée par des ténors comme Volkswagen.
Dans un entretien accordé à Autocar, Thomas Schäfer, le PDG de Volkswagen, confirme une méthode dont l’efficacité n’est plus à prouver : « nous avons radicalement repensé les véhicules et travaillé avec des partenaires ici [en Europe] et là-bas [en Chine]. Nous avons mis au point des véhicules qui sont totalement compétitifs en termes de coûts sur le marché chinois [et] travaillons en étroite collaboration avec nos collègues chinois ».
« Une décision déjà actée » : où vont arriver les premières VW faites en Chine ?

Pour maintenir des performances commerciales optimales, la chose est effectivement tentante.

articles.title: Paris-based Naboo acquires UK meetings and events specialist pro-ven following €58.7 million Series B | EU-Startups
articles.summary:
Naboo, a Paris-based EventTech scale-up, has joined forces with UK specialist pro-ven, bringing together two of the Meetings and Events (M&E) sector’s prominent names.
Starting today, pro-ven becomes Naboo UK. Together, the combined entity now oversees €269 million ($300 million) in meetings and events worldwide. The acquisition was financed through an equal split of equity and debt. The move follows Naboo’s €58.7 million Series B funding round earlier this year, led by Lightspeed Venture Partners and existing investors Notion Capital, ISAI, and Ternel.
“The future category leader in the M&E spend management market will be a pure player. Both event planners and procurement leaders have very high expectations in terms of user experience, embedded compliance, payment simplification, spend analytics and transparency. It cannot be achieved as a side business by TMCs who are still very much focused on transforming the transient travel experience. Together with pro-ven, that is the leader we are building,” said Maxime Eduardo, co-founder and CEO of Naboo.
Founded in 2022 by Eduardo, Antoine Servant, Lucien Bredin, and Jean-Louis Villeminot, Naboo is a platform for booking, managing, and running corporate events, also known as MICE (Meetings, Incentives, Conferences, and Exhibitions). articles.title: GPT-6.1 Terra : la nouvelle IA d’OpenAI qui veut révolutionner l’analyse du monde réel
articles.summary:
À partir d'une photographie ou d'un plan d'architecte, GPT-6.1 Terra peut retrouver un produit dans un catalogue ou construire une maquette 3D à l'écran, affirme OpenAI. On ne parle pas ici uniquement de reconnaissance visuelle, mais aussi et surtout du travail accompli ensuite dans les logiciels.
Après la présentation de GPT-6.1 Sol en septembre, OpenAI a lancé Terra. La présentation officielle affiche sa promesse en anglais, « From visual understanding to action », soit « de la compréhension visuelle à l’action ». Le modèle doit interpréter des images du monde réel, puis utiliser un ordinateur pour effectuer les opérations demandées. L'agent doit accomplir une tâche dans un logiciel à partir des éléments observés, au lieu de simplement commenter l'image. Le laboratoire n'a toutefois pas publié d'évaluation indépendante de ces usages.
Des images du monde réel aux logiciels de création
Avec un plan d'architecte, GPT-6.1 Terra doit reconnaître les formes représentées, puis manipuler un logiciel de modélisation pour construire un modèle en trois dimensions. OpenAI a retenu cet exercice dans ses évaluations des agents informatiques. L'agent doit donc accomplir une succession d'opérations à l'écran, et le résultat doit respecter les indications du plan original. Une image de bâtiment produite à partir du plan ne suffirait donc pas à accomplir le travail demandé.

articles.title: Firefox’s Smart Window adds AI form filling and webpage monitoring
articles.summary:
Mozilla is updating Smart Window — Firefox’s AI-powered browsing experience — with a new feature that can help you fill out online forms based on your open tabs. As an example, Mozilla says Smart Window can pull information from your online portfolio or LinkedIn page to paste your work history into a job application.
Firefox’s Smart Window adds AI form filling and webpage monitoring
An update to Firefox’s AI browsing experience can draw from your open tabs to help you fill out forms.
You can try out this feature by clicking into a form with at least four text fields. From there, you’ll see an option to “Fill from sources,” which will show all of the tabs Firefox will draw from. You can then select or deselect tabs that you want Firefox to use, and the browser will generate suggestions based on the information in them. This feature currently supports text fields on web forms, but Mozilla is working to add support for dropdown menus and PDFs. Mozilla notes that data from your source pages is shared with Google’s Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite, the AI model that generates the text suggestions.
Along with this update, you can now ask Firefox’s Smart Window to watch a certain webpage for sales, new job listings, and other updates. You can set up a task by typing “/watch” in the Smart Window chat, describing what you’re looking for, and adding the webpages you want to watch. Firefox can then check for updates on a daily or weekly basis, but only when the browser is open.

Introducing the Cloudflare PHP Capture the Flag challenge
Last week was one for the Internet security history books. First, eight eMudhra intermediate certificates were compromised, creating the possibility of forged certificates that could be used to impersonate servers. Then came php2shell: serious vulnerabilities in PHP, the runtime behind a large portion of the Web.
Cloudflare worked around the clock as these events unfolded to protect our customers and help protect the Internet. We shipped client updates and multiple mitigations, updated our web application firewall (WAF) with new rules to block attackers from exploiting the PHP vulnerabilities, and introduced a new feature called full transaction detection.
As always in situations like this, these new capabilities were made available on all plans, including Free.
Put our WAF to the test
Protecting systems from vulnerabilities like these is always an ongoing process, not a one-time event. The widespread adoption of AI allows attackers to discover new vectors with unprecedented speed and efficiency, so collecting real-world data to test our assumptions and strengthen defenses is essential.
That’s why today we're launching the Cloudflare PHP Capture the Flag challenge, run through our Bug Bounty program. We've put a deliberately vulnerable PHP installation behind our WAF, and we're inviting security researchers on HackerOne to try to bypass the protections and capture a flag.

articles.title: This is Fine: What NetScaler Zero-Days Tell Us About the New Normal
articles.summary:
If you’ve been paying attention to enterprise edge security lately, the September 2026 Citrix NetScaler zero-day advisories probably gave you a familiar case of heartburn. But before everyone panics, let’s step back and look at the bigger picture: what we are seeing right now isn’t a collapse of edge defense. It is, in fact, exactly how modern active defense is supposed to work when high-value, internet-facing infrastructure comes under heavy fire.
First, a quick refresher on why Citrix NetScaler ADC (Application Delivery Controller) and Gateway sit directly in the crosshairs of global threat actors. NetScaler is an everything-at-the-edge solution. It acts as a reverse proxy, load balancer, Web Application Firewall (WAF), traditional firewall, and SSL VPN all rolled into one appliance. Pretty much every major vendor in the perimeter space (F5, Cisco, Palo Alto Networks, Juniper, and more) went down this path of consolidation over the last decade or so. Instead of managing a bunch of standalone boxes chaining together these individual security controls, larger organizations clearly are showing a preference for a single platform to handle edge traffic. After all, it tends to be cheaper and easier to deploy just the one physical or virtual box from one vendor than to manage a constellation of security control devices.
The trade-off, however, is that spies and extortionists love this architectural shift just as much as IT departments do. If an attacker lands root on an edge devic…

- Date:

- Source:

- A new study reveals that people draw a surprisingly sharp line between human consciousness and artificial intelligence, even when both behave identically. Researchers found that participants considered even the most responsive AI less conscious than the least responsive human. Yet when asked about "awareness" instead, people judged humans and AI much more similarly.

Even when artificial intelligence behaves exactly like a human, people are reluctant to consider it conscious, according to a new study from Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (LMU).
As artificial intelligence becomes more advanced, reports of AI systems misleading users, working together, or appearing to pursue independent goals are becoming increasingly common. These behaviors often lead people to describe AI as though it can think, feel, or make decisions for itself. But does behaving like a human actually convince people that a machine has consciousness?
New research from LMU suggests that people make a clear distinction between displaying intelligent behavior and possessing a conscious mind, even when humans and AI act in precisely the same way.

articles.summary:
The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has added two critical PHP vulnerabilities collectively tracked as PHP2Shell to its catalog of actively exploited security flaws.
Threat actors without privileges can exploit the two security issues (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) in high-complexity attacks to gain remote code execution (RCE) on unpatched systems.
The PHP security team patched the two flaws on Wednesday, October 21, one day after urging security teams to install the security updates as soon as they became available.
Although details on the PHP2Shell security flaws (including the CVE IDs and mitigation measures shared with critical infrastructure providers) leaked and some proof-of-concept (PoC) exploits were published online before patches went live, the PHP security team said that none were functional.
Multiple cybersecurity firms (including Cloudflare, Amazon, Hadrian, watchTowr, Previdian, and Patchstack) also detected widespread exploitation attempts before public disclosure, but they all tagged them as unsuccessful.
Amazon Threat Intelligence security researchers also said that attackers began targeting the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities four days before security patches were released.

The same goes for scaling up quantum computing, yet progress is still often only measured in raw qubit count and fidelities. Those are key, of course, but by themselves they fail to tell you what amount of useful compute power your system brings. In the end, we’re pushing our technology to get it to a useful scale, which in the most basic sense means that value per solution must outweigh cost per solution.
Quantum computers hold real promise in utility applications, be it in faster drug discovery, accelerating materials research, or enabling more efficient machine learning once they run at a useful scale. Getting there means taking the cost of running these machines as seriously as the physics behind them to make them economical. A better understanding of how much useful compute power systems generate for each unit of energy or dollar you put into it is key for that.
At utility scale, compute per watt is what counts
There are two parts of that equation. The denominator is power: Cooling and control electronics in a quantum computer draw power continuously. articles.title: La Seguridad Social deja sin pensión de jubilación a un autónomo de 69 años en Baleares por las cuotas impagadas
articles.summary:
El 13 de marzo de 2024 Adriano, un trabajador autónomo que por entonces tenía 67 años, acudió a las oficinas del Instituto Nacional de Seguridad Social (INSS) para presentar los papeles de su jubilación. Quería retirarse. Y cobrar su pensión, claro. En los archivos del organismo figuran altas de Adriano en el Régimen Especial de Trabajadores Autónomos (RETA) que se remontan al menos a 1974, con lo que en teoría a sus 67 años cumpliría todos los requisitos.
El problema es que no es así. Para su sorpresa, la Seguridad Social respondió al trabajador que únicamente tenía cotizados 4.203 días, muy por debajo de los 5.475 (15 años) necesarios para acceder a la pensión de jubilación.
¿Cómo es posible ese desfase? Muy sencillo. Adriano quizás llevase décadas dado de alta en el RETA, pero no siempre estuvo al corriente de sus cuotas de autónomo. Y eso ha acabado afectando al período de cotización oficial.
El caso de Adriano lo conocemos gracias a una resolución publicada en la web del Consejo General del Poder Judicial (CGPJ), un documento que permite seguir capítulo a capítulo el culebrón burocrático-legal que ha seguido este sexagenario. articles.title: Relatório da ONU revela novo recorde de gases de efeito estufa
articles.summary:
A concentração de gases de efeito estufa na atmosfera atingiu níveis recordes em 2025, segundo relatório da Organização Meteorológica Mundial (OMM), divulgado nesta terça-feira (27). O acúmulo desses gases aumenta a retenção de calor no planeta e contribui para o aquecimento global.
O dióxido de carbono (CO₂) chegou a 426,8 partes por milhão, enquanto o metano e o óxido nitroso também atingiram máximas históricas. A OMM prevê que a concentração de CO₂ continuará aumentando em 2026.
CO₂ se acumula em ritmo acelerado
Em 2025, a concentração média global de dióxido de carbono chegou a 426,8 partes por milhão (ppm), equivalente a 153% do nível registrado em 1750, antes da industrialização. Isso significa que aproximadamente 427 de cada milhão de moléculas presentes no ar eram de CO₂.
O aumento em relação a 2024 foi de 2,8 ppm. Embora menor que no ano anterior, o avanço mantém a concentração em níveis elevados. Desde a década de 1960, o ritmo de crescimento do gás na atmosfera triplicou: passou de uma média de 0,8 ppm por ano naquele período para 2,4 ppm anuais entre 2011 e 2020. Em 2004, quando a OMM começou a publicar seu boletim sobre gases de efeito estufa, a concentração global era de 377,5 ppm.
“Mais um ano, mais um novo recorde. Os gases de efeito estufa estão retendo uma quantidade sem precedentes de calor na atmosfera, fornecendo energia para fenômenos meteorológicos mais extremos e aumentando os riscos para nossas economias e sociedades”, afirmou Ko Barrett, vice-secretá…

articles.title: One pod, one node: The architecture behind serverless Kubernetes on AWS
articles.summary:
One pod, one node: The architecture behind serverless Kubernetes on AWS
A pod-level walkthrough of admission routing, dedicated scheduling, and network isolation, no worker nodes required
Serverless Kubernetes changes who manages the node, not what Kubernetes expects from it. Kubernetes expects a node to register with the control plane, report capacity, run a Kubelet, provide networking, and host workloads. AWS Fargate provides those behaviors without asking customers to create, patch, scale, or replace a fleet of worker nodes.
Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS) Fargate solves that problem by making the pod the unit of infrastructure. When a pod is selected for Fargate, EKS provisions a dedicated compute environment, boots the Kubernetes components it needs, gives the pod an Elastic Network Interface (ENI) in the customer’s virtual private cloud (VPC), and tears the environment down when the pod is gone.
“Serverless Kubernetes changes who manages the node, not what Kubernetes expects from it.”
That customer experience depends on several coordinated design choices. Admission-time routing prevents the default scheduler from claiming a Fargate pod. A Fargate-specific scheduler provisions capacity instead of selecting from a pre-existing node pool. A focused runtime image supplies the Kubernetes node components, while separate network namespaces keep the platform path distinct from the workload path. articles.title: "Se acabó, la IA ganó": Google Gemini 4 Argon destruye una conjetura de fusión nuclear de 59 años en solo unas pocas horas

Gemini 4 Argon de Google ha ayudado a descubrir nuevas soluciones matemáticas relacionadas con la fusión nuclear. Los primeros candidatos se encontraron en cuestión de horas, según los investigadores. Esto supone una mejora con respecto al trabajo anterior, que refutó una conjetura formulada en 1967. Las aplicaciones prácticas se refieren a las pruebas del software que simula campos magnéticos para la investigación en fusión.
La conjetura lleva el nombre del físico Harold Grad. Aborda las ecuaciones que rigen el equilibrio del plasma y el campo magnético que lo rodea. El objetivo es identificar equilibrios estacionarios tridimensionales compatibles con un conjunto dado de condiciones de presión y simetría.
Cómo se encontraron las nuevas soluciones
La investigación que se publicó en arXiv es el resultado del esfuerzo conjunto de Opal Issan, Jonathan Citrin, Matt Landreman y Brendan Tracey. Los autores generalizaron las dos familias de soluciones anteriores mediante un parámetro en cada una, que rompe la simetría de stellarator. Los stellarators son dispositivos de fusión que utilizan campos magnéticos tridimensionales para contener el plasma.
Con el fin de encontrar generalizaciones de las familias de soluciones conocidas, los autores entregaron la investigación de Landreman y sus preguntas abiertas a un pequeño equipo de agentes de Gemini 4 en Google Antigravity. ENGIE operates in renewable energy, infrastructure, and customer energy supply in 30 countries, employs over 90,000 people, and reported €71.9 billion in revenue last year.
An ENGIE spokesperson told BleepingComputer that it cut off the attackers' access to the compromised platform and that they didn't breach the company's internal systems.
"ENGIE's internal IT systems were not compromised. ENGIE recently identified unusual data access activity within a tool used by partners as part of their customer prospecting activities and the marketing of energy offers," the spokesperson said.
The ENGIE spokesperson didn't say how many customers were affected, but told BleepingComputer the incident is limited to customers in France.

articles.title: Le nouvel Outlook est sur le point d’intégrer une fonction de réponse automatique
articles.summary:
Le client de messagerie de Microsoft s’apprête à combler l’une de ses plus grandes lacunes. Après plusieurs mois de test, la firme de Redmond est en effet sur le point d’intégrer une nouvelle fonctionnalité permettant de créer des règles pour répondre automatiquement aux e-mails que vous recevez dans Outlook.
Des règles de réponses automatiques basées sur des modèles
Au cours des prochaines semaines, le nouvel Outlook, mais aussi sa déclinaison web, vous permettra de créer des règles pour vos réponses automatiques. Concrètement, vous pourrez enregistrer des modèles de réponses à utiliser et à envoyer à certains contacts, en créant des règles. Dès lors que les conditions que vous avez définies sont remplies (lorsque certains mots spécifiques sont détectés dans le mail entrant, par exemple), Outlook pourra sélectionner le modèle de réponse adéquat pour répondre à votre place.
« Vous pouvez désormais créer une règle qui répond automatiquement aux messages entrants à l’aide d’un modèle que vous avez configuré. articles.title: When “isolated” doesn’t mean isolated: How to sandbox AI agents
articles.summary:
When “isolated” doesn’t mean isolated: How to sandbox AI agents
Separation of workloads before AI wasn’t easy, but it was far more straightforward. Servers sat in data centers, VLANs segregated packets, firewall rules managed ingress/egress, and physical cables separated packets to and from their destinations.
Now, flip on an agent, and it has access to almost everything by default.
Enterprises cannot operate with that default, and in this article, you’ll learn how to implement true sandboxing at every layer that matters.
Why aren’t containers enough to sandbox AI agents?
When you run a container (think Docker), it’s a lightweight package that runs as an isolated process. But that isolation has limits. Containers share the host kernel, and those on Docker’s default bridge can communicate with one another. A container cannot directly access host files by default, but a writable bind mount can let it modify or delete the host files exposed through that mount.
If you rely on a container alone for agent isolation, you may leave important boundaries unprotected. Thinking of containers as locked down by default is a major security risk. When running workloads in Kubernetes, you have tools like NetworkPolicy, service mesh for secure service communication, and SecurityContext to ensure containers run in a governed way.

articles.title: Hiding Capabilities in AI Models - Schneier on Security
articles.summary:
Hiding Capabilities in AI Models
Interesting research: “AI Models Can Provably Hide Arbitrary Capabilities”
Abstract: Capability evaluations aim to surface dangerous model behaviors before deployment, but their reliability depends on the assumption that hidden capabilities can be elicited. We show this assumption does not hold under adversarial conditions by constructing backdoor attacks that embed encrypted neural networks within host model weights, decrypting and executing them only upon receiving a secret trigger. Using digital lockers, these hidden circuits remain provably hard to elicit and interpret under cryptographic assumptions, even given full access to model weights, extending prior work from hiding fixed strings to arbitrary computations. We implement our proof of concept constructions in PyTorch and evaluate elicitation through fine-tuning, weight noising, gradient-based trigger search, and latent adversarial training, using a small chemical reaction prediction task as a proxy for CBRN-relevant capabilities. Our results demonstrate resistance to these methods and, together with our cryptographic guarantees, reveal a limit of elicitation-based capability audits. We release our models to support the improvement of defenses.

articles.title: Unexplained DreamHost Incident Prompts Email, FTP Password Resets
articles.summary:
Over the weekend, web hosting provider DreamHost suspended its File Manager service and reset some user passwords.
The company says it took protective actions in response to “an issue” with its systems, which affected File Manager at files.dreamhost.com and DreamHost webmail.
“As a precaution, we are resetting passwords for some email and FTP/SFTP users,” the company warned on Friday.
It also notified DreamHost account owners via private communication (shared on Reddit), noting that users would need to set new passwords when logging in, and underlining that DreamHost would not request password resets via email.
“We are contacting you because you are the DreamHost account owner, and only you will be able to set new passwords for these users. DreamHost is unable to contact individual mailbox or FTP users directly, so they may not know about this until you tell them,” the company said.
“If they used the old password anywhere else, they should change it there too,” DreamHost told account owners.
Users complained about DreamHost’s lack of transparency, and some speculated that the passwords may have been compromised and questioned whether they were properly hashed.
In the meantime, DreamHost says it has created and deployed a fix to the File Manager and restored access to http://files.dreamhost.com.
“We are monitoring the situation to ensure that the File Manager is back in a fully operational state,” the company said on Monday.

articles.title: Apple backports CoreGraphics zero-day patches to older iPhones
articles.summary:
Apple has backported security patches released last month to older iPhones and iPads, addressing a zero-day bug exploited in "extremely sophisticated" targeted attacks on iOS devices.
Apple patched the same vulnerability in September for devices running iOS 26.7.1 and iPadOS 26.7.1, macOS Tahoe 26.7.1, and macOS Sequoia 15.8.1.
Meta Product Security discovered this out-of-bounds write weakness (tracked as CVE-2026-86950) in CoreGraphics, a framework used for two-dimensional vector graphics, text drawing, and image rendering across iOS, macOS, iPadOS, watchOS, and tvOS.
Successful exploitation of out-of-bounds write security issues can let attackers crash programs, corrupt data, or gain remote code execution by writing data outside the allocated memory buffer.
"Apple is aware of a report that this issue may have been exploited in an extremely sophisticated attack against specific targeted individuals on versions of iOS before iOS 27," Apple warned on Monday.
"Processing a maliciously crafted file may lead to arbitrary code execution. An out-of-bounds write issue was addressed with improved bounds checking."
With this week's security patches, Apple has now also addressed this vulnerability on iPhone XS, iPhone XS Max, iPhone XR, iPad 7th generation, iPad Air 4th generation and later, iPad 9th generation and later, and iPad mini 6th generation and later.

articles.title: Impressionnant, l'Airbus H140 a passé l'épreuve américaine en résistant à la chaleur extrême et à la haute altitude
articles.summary:
Airbus Helicopters a achevé aux États-Unis une campagne d'essais dite « hot and high » de son nouvel hélicoptère H140, résistant aux 45°C au-delà du désert et à près de 4 000 mètres dans les Rocheuses.
Le nouvel hélicoptère H140 d’Airbus Helicopters a bouclé le 8 octobre près de quatre mois d’essais en vol aux États-Unis, une étape très importante sur le chemin de la certification. La campagne, qui a eu lieu du 13 juin au 8 octobre 2026 très précisément, a prouvé que l'appareil peut garder la tête froide, sans mauvais jeu de mots, quand l'air devient brûlant ou qu'il se raréfie. Le dernier-né d'Airbus Helicopters a encaissé une température de 45 °C puis frôlé les 4 000 mètres dans les Rocheuses du Colorado. Son ingénieur en chef, Christian Wehle, raconte la campagne marathon de l'hélicoptère, dont les premières livraisons sont visées en 2028.
Pourquoi l'Airbus H140 est allé chercher la chaleur et l’altitude
Les essais « hot and high », littéralement « chaud et haut », ont servi pour l'Airbus H140 à vérifier comment un hélicoptère se comporte quand la chaleur et l'altitude se liguent contre lui. Pour l'hélicoptère, on peut parler d'une étape clé de la certification, selon la formule consacrée. Mais pourquoi aller se faire griller en plein désert ? Parce qu'un hélicoptère n'aime pas l'air léger. Plus il fait chaud et plus on monte, plus l'air se raréfie, les pales y trouvent alors moins d'appui, et les moteurs y respirent moins bien. What did you see in those early days that told you there was a problem Kotani Pay could solve?
We started as a bunch of educators teaching people in Nairobi about blockchain, around 2018. We soon hit a problem: Africans pay through mobile money, and mobile money couldn’t connect to the blockchain. In one basic-income pilot in Nairobi’s informal settlements, people received digital money they couldn’t spend. A local agent swapped it for cash, and he quickly became a target.
We thought someone should be able to move from the blockchain to Kenya shillings, and from Kenya shillings back to the blockchain, using the readily available payment channel, which is mobile money. articles.title: Científicos reconstruyeron en 3D al carpintero más grande del mundo, extinto hace 70 años
articles.summary:
El carpintero imperial, el ave más grande de su familia, con una longitud de hasta 60 centímetros y un peso cercano a los 700 gramos, no ha sido visto en libertad desde 1956. Habitaba los bosques maduros de pinos de la Sierra Madre Occidental, en México, y su desaparición se atribuye a la tala masiva de esos ecosistemas.
Alrededor de un centenar de especímenes se conservan en museos de distintos países, y las únicas imágenes en movimiento de la especie son unos pocos segundos de una película filmada hace casi siete décadas.
Con ese material fragmentario como punto de partida, un equipo de investigadores construyó un modelo tridimensional animado del carpintero imperial a partir del escaneo de una piel de museo y de la única filmación silvestre disponible. La reconstrucción, que reproduce tanto el vuelo como el ascenso por un tronco, fue concebida como un recurso científico reproducible y de acceso abierto, disponible para descarga por parte de cualquier persona.
El trabajo, liderado por Joshua Medina, de la Universidad de Massachusetts Amherst, contó con la colaboración del Laboratorio Moore de Zoología del Occidental College en Los Ángeles y de la Universidad Estatal de Oregón. Fue publicado en la revista Natural History Collections and Museomics.
El escaneo de 288 fotografías permitió reconstruir el cuerpo con precisión submilimétrica

articles.title: The Huntress Tragic Quadrant: Ranking Threats Hitting Businesses Hardest

Cyber headlines often focus on the flashy attacks, but the ones that actually cause OH $#!T moments are the tactics that abuse the tools and workflows you already trust. If you run a small or mid-sized organization, whether you handle IT yourself or outsource it, it’s a constant race to keep up with attackers and their evolving tactics.
The bottom line is that you need to know which attacks are landing in environments like yours, and how to prioritize your defenses against them.
The Tragic Quadrant at a Glance
That’s why Huntress created the Tragic Quadrant, a ranked list of the cyber tactics putting businesses at risk, built to show you where to focus regardless of what’s trending week to week.
Fix These Threats First: The OH $#!T Corner
Each of these tactics hides inside something your team uses every day, like a remote access tool or a Microsoft 365 login.
RMM Abuse Is Steady and Holding
Remote monitoring and management (RMM) tools are a staple for IT teams, which is exactly why attackers abuse them. One rogue RMM install gives an attacker persistent access that looks like ordinary admin work.
In Q1 2026, 45% of endpoint-related incidents Huntress investigated involved RMM abuse. Attackers are also using AI to build convincing fake document shares and service agreement lures that trick users into installing unwanted RMMs.

The slop extends to legal work
AI was supposed to make work easier, but now many are grappling with what Jamie Bartlett, author and BBC journalist, describes as “the burden of AI clog“. Cleaning up this mess means that AI is not saving time, but is actually creating more work.
The slop extends to the legal domain, with contract negotiations and other legal work now being absorbed by a lengthy review process because of AI. Even the bodies that are supposed to be drafting the laws are swimming in slop. In the US, for example, the Office of the Legislative Counsel, is reportedly overwhelmed by the error-riddled drafts that AI has generated.
The problem isn’t AI per se
Advances in LegalTech in Europe, and beyond, means there are many tools to assist with legal work. Despite this, however, their output is of varying quality. And some law firms still don’t have a proper policy in place for how employees use AI, which means some teams are relying on general LLMs (like ChatGPT or Claude) for their drafting and reviewing.

In its latest gift to oil and gas companies, the Trump administration is expected to announce plans today to weaken rules that guard against methane leaks.
Trump is making it easier for fossil fuel companies to leak methane
The Environmental Protection Agency is lowering standards meant to keep methane from leaking from oil and gas infrastructure.
Methane is a smog-forming pollutant and a powerful greenhouse gas that’s up to 80 times as potent as carbon dioxide on a 20-year horizon. It’s the primary component of what the fossil fuel industry calls “natural gas” that routinely leaks from oil and gas wells and pipelines.
The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is reversing course on its previous efforts to plug those leaks. As part of President Donald Trump’s deregulatory agenda, the EPA plans to undo Biden-era rules that were expected to cut methane emissions by 80 percent over 14 years.
Methane has caused about 30 percent of global warming
The EPA teased the rule change earlier this month, saying in a press release that it was “days away” from making the proposal. EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin says the rollbacks will save oil and gas companies $45 billion, while the previous rules would have incurred $18 billion in regulatory costs.

A swimming robot does not necessarily need a bulky motor or powerful mechanical parts to move through water. MIT researchers have demonstrated that a single, carefully engineered layer of living muscle cells can generate enough force to propel a tiny robot forward.
The engineers developed an extremely thin swimming robot that uses living muscle tissue to move its fins. Described in a new study published in Advanced Functional Materials, the device has a flexible gel framework roughly the length and width of a stick of gum. The gel forms two fins, each coated with a layer of muscle cells far thinner than a human hair. These cells have been genetically modified to contract when exposed to light.

Tailscale develops a software-defined mesh virtual private network (VPN) built on WireGuard that lets users connect computers, servers, and cloud instances from anywhere to the same encrypted mesh network ("tailnet") via direct peer-to-peer (P2P) connections.
Cyberdione Labs discovered 11 flaws (collectively known as Tailworm) that still lack patches during a security audit of Tailscale 1.104.2 and the self-hosted headscale v0.29.5 control server.
"All findings were verified by reproduction in a lab environment on unmodified, released software (tailscale v1.104.2, headscale v0.29.5)," said Erica Windisch, founder of Cyberdione Labs, who reported the flaws to Tailscale and publicly released the details.
"It is the opinion of the researchers that rapid awareness of these flaws will expediate remediation across impacted devices. These vulnerabilities were not introduced by the researchers, but were discovered, and discovered with low effort."

articles.title: The hidden failure paths that affect Kubernetes control plane availability
articles.summary:
The hidden failure paths that affect Kubernetes control plane availability
Kubernetes control planes are designed to contain individual failures, but their availability still depends on how components in the critical path behave under pressure. At fleet scale, a component does not have to crash to contribute to an outage. A valid mechanism can amplify a local defect through shared metadata, synchronized startup work, or an overly aggressive health check.
For example, an informer gives a controller a local view of cluster state, letting its workers make progress without repeatedly querying the API server. This is efficient when controllers start independently. When many controllers restart simultaneously across a fleet, rebuilding those views can place significant pressure on the control plane. The informer mechanism itself becomes the amplifier.
“At fleet scale, a component does not have to crash to contribute to an outage. A valid mechanism can amplify a local defect through shared metadata, synchronized startup work, or an overly aggressive health check.”
This article examines three cases. In the first, an extension API server published an invalid schema after a dependency upgrade and blocked clients that had never used its API. In the second, DaemonSet agents restarted across a large fleet, turning routine startup work into a request storm the API server couldn’t absorb. In the third, a deep liveness check on a component in the API request path treated a dependency outage …

Para abordar ese desafío, se han creado opciones como una arquitectura y un conjunto de herramientas para que las protecciones de seguridad dejen de depender de cada aplicación individual y se apliquen desde las capas más profundas de la plataforma tecnológica.
El modelo, denominado Deep Trust AI Architecture, parte de una premisa concreta: si las políticas de acceso y las reglas de negocio se definen solo en el código de cada aplicación, los sistemas generados por IA pueden implementarlas mal o, en el peor de los casos, saltarlas por completo. La propuesta traslada esas protecciones a cuatro niveles de la infraestructura (software base, datos, acceso a los datos y desarrollo de aplicaciones) para que todo agente o aplicación que opere sobre esa plataforma las herede de forma automática.

articles.title: Tailscale Rushes Patches After Uncoordinated Disclosure of ‘Tailworm’ Flaws
articles.summary:
Tailscale is getting ready to ship a client update that addresses privilege escalation weaknesses in Tailscale SSH. Details of the bugs went public over the weekend.
Tailscale provides a mesh VPN service that uses the WireGuard protocol to connect an organization’s devices and services over a private, peer-to-peer network.
The Tailscale vulnerabilities, dubbed Tailworm, are described in a report from Cyberdione Labs. It lists 11 findings affecting version 1.104.2 of the Tailscale client and version 0.29.5 of headscale, an open source control server that organizations can host themselves.
Cyberdione Labs published the report before any patches were available, drawing criticism on social media, though the researchers argued that rapid awareness would speed up remediation.
Six of the findings are rated high severity, and four of them concern Tailscale SSH, which grants access based on device identity and network policy instead of passwords or keys.
According to the Tailworm report, Tailscale SSH performs some forwarding operations with root privileges, and the safeguards meant to restrict them can be bypassed.
An attacker who has compromised one device could exploit this against any server that device is permitted to reach over Tailscale SSH, as long as the access rule allows forwarding. In lab tests, this resulted in root access on target servers and the theft of keys that can be used to add rogue devices to the network.

articles.title: Microsoft releases Windows OOB updates to distrust eMudhra certificates
articles.summary:
Microsoft has released out-of-band (OOB) Windows updates to remove trust in certificates tied to compromised eMudhra certificate authority keys, protecting systems that do not receive automatic certificate trust updates.
The KB5134133 update for Windows 11 versions 24H2, 25H2, and 26H2 and the KB5134125 update for Windows 10 versions 21H2 and 22H2 were released on October 26.
The updates are for systems without Internet access, devices that cannot access Microsoft's certificate-update service, and those where automatic Certificate Trust List (CTL) updates have been disabled.
The updates were released after the discovery of eight eMudhra intermediate certificate authority private keys that were so weak they could be recovered almost instantly.
All eight keys were generated in April 2025 and had values smaller than 256, allowing anyone to recover them by testing just 256 possible numbers.
The compromised keys could have allowed attackers to forge certificates for legitimate websites and intercept encrypted communications.
After the disclosure, eMudhra revoked the eight compromised intermediate certificates, and Mozilla, Google, Apple, and other software vendors also began revoking them.
In response, Microsoft previously updated the Windows Disallowed Certificate Trust List to block the eight affected intermediate certificate authorities, including six used for TLS and two for code signing.

Bis die Glasfaserinfrastruktur großflächig etabliert ist, könnte das Mobilfunknetz einspringen, um Breitbandinternet zu liefern. Dies schlägt jedenfalls das deutsche Beratungsunternehmen Dialog Consult in einer Studie vor.
5G Fixed-Wireless-Access kann auf bestehende Struktur zurückgreifen
Dialog Consult setzt genauer gesagt auf 5G Fixed-Wireless-Access (5G FWA). Dabei wird Breitbandinternet über das Mobilfunknetz an einen festen Standort geliefert. Kabel müssen dazu nicht verlegt werden.
Der Vorteil: Die Infrastruktur besteht bereits. Gebäude müssten nur mit einem 5G-Router oder einer Außenantenne nachgerüstet werden.
5G als Ergänzung und Übergangslösung für Glasfaser
Die Autoren betonen, dass sie Glasfaser nicht zugunsten von 5G aufgeben wollen. Sie sehen den Standard eher als Ergänzung und Übergangslösung.
So könnte 5G die Zeit überbrücken, bis großflächig Glasfaserkabel verlegt sind. In Gegenden, in denen sich der Ausbau von Glasfasertechnologie wirtschaftlich nicht lohnt, könnte 5G FWA sogar dauerhaft eine alternative Lösung darstellen.
In Österreich kommt laut der Studie bereits im großen Stil Fixed-Wireless-Access zum Einsatz. Die Hälfte aller Breitbandanschlüsse läuft im Nachbarland über 4G oder 5G. Dies gelte vor allem für ländliche Gegenden.…

Engineers from Amazon Web Services (AWS) have described how the team that maintains the Linux kernel for EC2 infrastructure handles kernel CVEs. The process combines an automated filter, an AI agent and human review. The team also argues that it needs to move to newer long-term-support (LTS) kernels, as older branches collect fixes that are never backported.
Dylan Johnson and Justinien Bouron gave the talk at the Linux Plumbers Conference in Prague earlier this month. At the start of the recording, Johnson explains that the team maintains the kernel used within EC2 infrastructure. This is separate from Amazon Linux and from the kernels that customers run in their virtual machines.
After the kernel project became a CVE Numbering Authority in February 2024, the team saw about two kernel CVEs a week before 2024 and about 16 a day afterwards, with 848 published on 15 August 2026. The kernel CVE documentation states that the project cannot know how a given system uses the kernel, so users must decide which CVEs apply to them.
The first stage of AWS's process does not use AI. Bouron explained that kernel CVE records are published in JSON and list the affected versions and source files. A script discards a CVE if the kernel version is outside the affected range, or if none of the listed files are built into the image. In AWS's environment this removes about 70% of CVEs, although Bouron said the figure depends heavily on kernel configuration.
The remaining CVEs go to an AI agent. It …
