articles.title: Modders unlock hidden AI power on Nvidia RTX 20, 30, and 40 series GPUs, nearly doubling some benchmarks
articles.summary:
Sounding off: A used RTX 3090 has become the go-to card for running AI models at home, mostly because 24GB of memory costs far less on a gaming card than on a workstation one. That bargain comes with a catch Nvidia prints in its own spec sheets, though. On GeForce cards, one of the most common kinds of AI math runs at exactly half speed. A few open-source projects now claim to remove that limitation on RTX 20-, 30-, and 40-series cards.
The limit lives in the tensor cores. When they multiply FP16 or BF16 numbers and add up the results in higher-precision FP32, GeForce cards issue those instructions at half the rate of the FP16-accumulate mode. That FP32 mode is the one most training and plenty of inference actually rely on. The workstation cards Nvidia builds on the same chips – the RTX A6000, for example – run it at full speed.
The first fix came from GitHub user Zagitta, who published "gpu-unlock" for RTX 30-series cards. It's a Linux kernel module that kicks in before Nvidia's driver loads. That's when it rewrites two speed-select registers on the GPU and resets the card. Nvidia's regular driver then takes over as usual, so nobody has to flash a VBIOS or patch a driver.
On an RTX 3090 Ti capped at 450W, the developer's matrix-multiply tests show BF16 throughput climbing from 87.5 to 157.4 TFLOPS. TF32 nearly doubled, too. FP16 saw a smaller gain of 35%.

articles.title: Nebius cut rollout collection time by 66.9% — here’s what changed
articles.summary:
Nebius cut rollout collection time by 66.9% — here’s what changed
In AI agent training, you can pay for powerful GPUs and still spend much of your time waiting. Agents need to attempt tasks and produce results before the model can learn from them. A few slow attempts can hold up the next training update, making the systems that run those tasks a major factor in training speed and cost.
Di Jin, VP of AI Training at Amsterdam-headquartered Nebius, says teams coming from pretraining or supervised fine-tuning can underestimate the work these systems do.
“If you staff and design it as a training project, inference becomes the bottleneck nobody owns.”
Rollout generation often takes most of a training step’s wall-clock time, making batching, cache management and scheduling central to how fast the model can learn. “If you staff and design it as a training project, inference becomes the bottleneck nobody owns,” Jin says.
Time to a trainable batch
He adds that engineers should measure time to a trainable batch alongside throughput. Average tokens per second can hide the long tail: in a synchronous batch, the step cannot finish until the final trajectory is completed.
Agent trajectories do not all have the same length. Many finish quickly, while others take longer, leaving training GPUs waiting on a handful of stragglers. For this reason, Jin advises engineers to treat the inference engine as part of the post-training reinforcement learning optimizer.

Apocalyptic warnings about AI are a dime a dozen, but they hit a lot harder when one comes from an expert in the field. Soares has spent 12 years working on AI alignment. articles.title: How Anthropic Redesigned Source Control for AI-Driven Development
articles.summary:
Anthropic recently detailed how it migrated its monorepo from Git to Scion. Scion is a source control system that moves repository operations to the server side and uses content-addressed storage and tiered caches for agent and CI workloads. The design sacrifices offline independence for less local data and shared infrastructure.
In its 13 October engineering post, Anthropic reported that daily merged changes rose from around 2,500 in May to more than 30,000 in September. Its CI systems perform approximately 25 million checkouts daily, against a monorepo with nearly 100 GB of main-branch history and a compressed working copy exceeding 25 GB. The company had used shallow clones, sparse checkouts, promisor remotes, repository snapshots and several hundred Git mirrors, but said these became harder to operate as merge rates increased.
Daily merged changes in Anthropic’s monorepo from January to September 2026. (Source)
Scion puts commits, merges, rebases, history and blame queries on the server. Clients maintain bounded object caches and virtualised checkouts materialise files on demand. Tools can query diffs and perform some writes through APIs without checking out code.
A Scion changeset records the files that have changed relative to its first parent, with content-addressed pointers to the compressed file contents in blob storage. Creating changesets is separate from updating references, so accepting changesets requires no cross-server coordination. For history and blame queri…

Uber has introduced Normalized Compute Units (NCUs) to make CPU allocation more consistent across its highly heterogeneous server fleet. The approach, implemented in Uber's Odin stateful orchestration platform, accounts for differences in processor performance rather than treating every CPU core as equivalent.
Odin manages around 5 million CPU cores across on-premises data centres and public clouds, including multiple generations of x86 hardware and ARM processors. Uber found that single-threaded performance can vary by almost a factor of two between the fastest and slowest cores. Consequently, the same workload can require significantly different numbers of physical CPU cores depending on where it runs.
The problem creates two competing risks. Allocating resources according to the slowest hardware can waste capacity on faster machines, while allocating according to average usage can leave workloads under-provisioned when they move to slower servers. For stateful workloads, where moving traffic to another machine is often not possible, the latter can become a reliability problem.
Uber's solution is to separate the amount of compute performance a workload requires from the physical cores used to provide it.
Odin assigns each server type a performance factor, using an older server generation as a baseline of 100. Newer hardware can have considerably higher values; Uber reports factors approaching 190 for some servers. These factors are initially determined during hardware quali…

YouTube prévoit de diffuser ses premières vidéos en AV2 dès 2027. Ce nouveau codec promet une compression environ 30 % plus efficace que l'AV1, mais les téléviseurs et box actuels risquent de ne jamais pouvoir en profiter pleinement. En cause : un décodage particulièrement exigeant, qui nécessitera probablement de nouvelles puces.
L'AV2 commence à prendre forme. Le 22 octobre, l'Alliance for Open Media (AOMedia) a confirmé que YouTube envisageait ses premiers flux utilisant ce codec dès le début de l'année 2027. Une avancée importante pour le streaming vidéo, mais qui ne concernera pas immédiatement nos téléviseurs. Google vise d'abord les navigateurs web, tandis qu'aucun calendrier n'a été annoncé pour les applications TV ou les box multimédias.
L'AV2 arrive sur YouTube, mais votre téléviseur devra patienter
Successeur de l'AV1, l'AV2 promet de réduire d'environ 30 % le débit nécessaire pour obtenir une qualité d'image comparable. Un avantage considérable pour les plateformes, qui pourraient économiser de la bande passante ou proposer une meilleure qualité vidéo à débit équivalent.
 Mais cette efficacité a une contrepartie : le codec est nettement plus exigeant à décoder.
Jean-Baptiste Kempf, président de VideoLAN, estime que le décodage AV2 est environ cinq fois plus complexe que celui de l'AV1. Les processeurs actuels peuvent théoriquement effectuer cette opération par logiciel, mais la lecture en temps réel, particulièrement en 4K, représente un défi important.

Quatre mois plus tard, le 1er juillet, cette taxe était supprimée et remplacée par des droits de douane européens de 3 € par catégorie, sur les colis de 150 € ou moins. Comme nous l’expliquions en juillet, un seul colis pouvait donc déjà cumuler 6, 9 ou 12 € de droits.
Cette fois, l’addition va encore grimper dès le 1er novembre avec de nouveaux frais de traitement européens de 2 € par catégorie d’article. Ces derniers ne remplacent pas la taxe déjà mise en place et s’ajouteront ainsi aux 3 € déjà appliqués.
Les mesures sont censées freiner l’afflux de petits colis venus de l’extérieur de l’Union européenne, notamment ceux commandés sur Shein, Temu ou AliExpress. Mais combien allez-vous payer au bout du compte, et cette accumulation de prélèvements règle-t-elle vraiment le problème ?
Les nouveaux frais de 2 € se calculent aussi par catégorie d’article
Officiellement appelée « frais de traitement de l’Union » (Union handling fee en anglais), cette redevance doit financer le travail des douanes : vérification des déclarations, analyse des risques et contrôles des marchandises. La Commission européenne en a fixé le montant par un acte délégué adopté le 21 septembre. La redevance s’appliquera dans toute l’Union européenne dès ce dimanche.

articles.title: "Puede devorar hasta 30 kg de pescado al día": el temor de los municipios catalanes ante la reintroducción de una criatura perdida hace 50 años
articles.summary:
En Cataluña han dado luz verde al regreso de una criatura que desapareció de sus costas hace más de medio siglo. El plan parece simple: traer focas monje desde África y devolverlas al Mediterráneo, empezando por algunos enclaves de la Costa Brava. La iniciativa promete recuperar una especie amenazada y restaurar parte del equilibrio ecológico perdido. El problema está en su apetito: según los pescadores y las autoridades locales, cada ejemplar adulto puede llegar a consumir hasta 30 kilos de pescado al día.
Dos municipios ya han dejado claro que no van a asumir las consecuencias.
Un regreso después de 50 años. La Generalitat quiere recuperar la foca monje del Mediterráneo (Monachus monachus), una especie que antiguamente habitaba las costas catalanas y cuya presencia fue disminuyendo durante el siglo XX. La caza, las capturas accidentales, la persecución por parte de pescadores y la transformación del litoral contribuyeron a su desaparición.
Uno de los últimos avistamientos documentados en el cabo de Creus se produjo en 1973, entre Roses y Cadaqués. El secretario de Transición Ecológica, Jordi Sargatal, lleva más de veinte años defendiendo su recuperación y quiere reactivar el proyecto en 2027, con el cabo de Creus y la isla balear de Cabrera entre los principales lugares considerados.

Developer notaroomba (AKA Nathan Alspaugh) has published details of his Keybytes project on GitHub. We’ve seen oodles of imaginative and truly excellent mechanical keyboards over recent years, but Keybytes probably offers the greatest flexibility with regard to layout and key selection we’ve ever seen.
It starts with a Keyword, which is the main board that the Keybits connect to. This central component houses a stacked pair of PCBs. The top board packs an Arm Cortex M4-powered microcontroller, Bluetooth antenna, and flash memory. The lower board offers USB-C, charging, and a buck-boost converter.

Was ist eigentlich das älteste Programm mit grafischer Oberfläche (GUI), das ohne Emulation oder Modifikation noch unter Windows 11 läuft? Dieser Frage widmete sich der Programmierer Boris Popik und kam zu einigen überraschenden Erkenntnissen.
Keine 16-Bit-Unterstützung in Windows 11
Wie Popik in seinem Blog erklärt, bietet Windows 11 keine native Unterstützung von 16-Bit-Anwendungen. Das bedeutet, dass die Suche erst in der frühen Windows-NT-Ära Anfang der 1990er-Jahre beginnen kann. Das von Microsoft entwickelte 32-Bit-Betriebssystem kam im Juli 1993 auf den Markt.
In einem Forum wurde Popik auf Win32s aufmerksam gemacht, einer Erweiterung für Windows 3.1 und Windows 3.11 und einer Art Brückentechnologie für den Übergang in das 32-Bit-Zeitalter. Mit Win32s war es möglich, bestimmte 32-Bit-Programme auf dem älteren 16-Bit-Windows zum Laufen zu bringen.
Freecell von 1993 zum Laufen gebracht
Zu den bekanntesten Anwendungen, die eine installierte Win32s-Umgebung voraussetzten, gehörte das Kartenspiel Freecell. Und genau hier wurde Popik fündig. Er brachte eine aus dem Februar 1993 stammende Freecell-Version unter Windows 11 zum Laufen, ohne irgendwelche Änderungen vornehmen zu müssen.

articles.title: Sculpture re-creates odd optical effects of famed Lycurgus Cup
articles.summary:
Dating back to around 400 CE and made of dichroic glass, the Lycurgus Cup is notable for exhibiting different colors depending on the light. (It gets its name from the scene depicted on its surface, of King Lycurgus of Thrace.) Light it from the front, and the cup looks green; light it from behind, and the color changes to a deep red. University of Sheffield scientists have re-created the original recipe to produce a contemporary glass sculpture with the same optical effect.
The cup is considered one of the seven glass wonders of the world, one of just 40 glass cage cups that survived. Exactly why the unusual color effects of the Lycurgus Cup occurred was a mystery until 2007, when a team of scientists discovered the color shifts were due to the presence of nanoparticles in the glass—the result of Roman artisans adding finely ground gold and silver into the mix. Those nanoparticles change how the electrons in the cup vibrate in response to light so that the color one sees shifts with the observer’s vantage point.
As we reported in 2019, it’s a similar phenomenon to the one responsible for the shifting colors of 19th-century daguerreotypes due to the scattering properties of nanoparticles. The Romans added salt when they melted the silicon (sand) to make the glass, and those salts contained gold atoms. In the melting process, those atoms aggregate and produce nanoparticles, which in turn produce the colors. It’s how any stained glass is made. It’s also similar to how the preci…

Essa não é a estreia de vídeos horizontais na plataforma e nem a primeira vez que o Instagram adapta uma ferramenta ao formato, mas, além do player, a rede deve integrar o formato aos Reels.
Criadores poderão publicar cortes e vinculá-los ao vídeo completo, permitindo que o usuário continue assistindo ao conteúdo sem sair do Instagram. O chefe da rede, Adam Mosseri, mostrou em um post como a ferramenta funciona.
Segundo a vice-presidente de produto Tessa Lyons, a intenção é criar uma porta de entrada para a produção principal. A empresa está testando a possibilidade de vincular até oito Reels a um mesmo vídeo longo.
O Features já vinha sendo testado com alguns criadores brasileiros e começou a chegar nesta semana a um grupo restrito nos Estados Unidos.
A iniciativa representa uma mudança de posição para a rede social, que sempre priorizou vídeos curtos. Segundo Lyons, o medo era de que os vídeos longos reduzissem as interações que a empresa considera centrais para a plataforma, como enviar Reels, fotos e carrosséis para amigos.

Que OpenAI o Anthropic salgan a buscar dinero es lo normal porque todo su negocio es la IA, partían de cero ingresos y han tenido que gastar (y siguen gastando) muchísimo antes de ingresar lo suficiente. Lo que es raro es ver en la misma cola para recaudar a dos empresones como Meta y Google.
Por qué es importante. Durante años, la ventaja de las grandes tecnológicas en la carrera de la IA ha sido muy simple: han podido pagársela de su bolsillo. Facebook, Instagram y WhatsApp (o Google y YouTube) generan tantísimo dinero con la publicidad que estas empresas han podido levantar centros de datos sin tener que pedirle nada a nadie.
Eso se ha acabado. En el último trimestre, Meta ha ingresado 64.600 millones, un 26% más que hace un año, y aun así su flujo de caja libre ha sido negativo. Ha gastado más de lo que le entra, y este año prevé invertir entre 135.000 y 145.000 millones.

The federal government is considering adding gaming platforms to its digital safety bill to stop predators from using those platforms to target kids.
There are a number of gaming platforms that allow adults to communicate with children, which has sparked concerns over predatory behaviours like grooming.
Roblox has become one of the chief platforms of concern, with about 40 per cent of the game’s over 85 million players being under the age of 13. A Canadian documentary from last year exposed the darker underside of Roblox, where bad actors targeted children with hateful content, and predators used the game to groom children.

I understand the appeal of foldable phones—they let manufacturers keep expanding screen sizes while still producing devices that can reasonably fit in a pocket. In practice, though, every foldable Android phone I’ve seen in public has had a ridiculously visible seam between the two halves of the screen, often with what looks like delamination from the underlying surface, giving the display an ugly, bubbly appearance.
Back when Android phones began shipping with bigger and bigger screens and the iPhone was stuck at a miserly four inches, I was jealous. But I’ve never looked at anyone using a chunky, fragile-looking foldable phone in public and pined for Apple’s take on the idea.
Nevertheless, that take has arrived, in the form of the iPhone Duo. This $1,999-and-up foldable is the biggest change to the iPhone in years, with both hardware and software updates that dramatically change how you interact with the device.
Like most Apple products, it looks and feels solid, and Apple has managed to engineer its way around at least some of the problems that have bedeviled other foldables (in particular, it has wrangled the between-screen crease so close to invisibility that I rarely thought about it while using the phone unfolded).

What matters is understanding the problems within the business that technology can genuinely help solve and having a clear way to measure whether it has made a difference. articles.title: Lo que Carl Jung puede enseñarnos sobre envejecer bien: "Deberíamos saber que hay un proceso interno e implacable que fuerza a restringir su vida"
articles.summary:
Desde hace tiempo, hay una frase de Carl Gustav Jung sobre la vejez que no deja de aparecer una y otra vez: que quien envejece debería saber que su vida ya no crece ni se ensancha, que hay "un proceso interno e implacable que fuerza a restringir su vida". Suena a taza de desayuno (si los fabricantes de tazas de desayuno tuvieran cierta tirria a la tercera edad) y a frase de autoayuda falsa que circula bajo firma ilustre. Pero no. Por una vez, es suya.
Paradójicamente, que sea de Jung no es garantía de nada. Por mucho cariño que le tengamos al viejo suizo, sigue siendo verdad que fue a casi todos los efectos un charlatán de intuición prodigiosa; pero charlatán al fin y al cabo. Un erudito esotérico cuyas teorías extienden cheques que la evidencia empírica no suele ser capaz de pagar.
Y esto es un buen ejemplo de sus limitaciones: durante décadas la psicología ha vuelto obsesivamente a esa idea (que, con los años, la vida social se encoge) y ha acabado dándole la razón en todo, menos en lo importante: y es que no es la edad lo que estrecha la vida, es el tiempo que creemos que nos queda.
¿Qué dijo exactamente Jung? La frase sale de 'Die Lebenswende', un ensayo que Jung presentó en 1930 y que, tras revisarlo a conciencia, acabó publicando en 'Seelenprobleme der Gegenwart' en 1931. Tenía 54 años y, desde hace tiempo, había una imagen que le obsesionaba: que la vida era como el arco que marca el sol en el firmamento.

articles.title: From cheap tool to premium subscription: When a beloved app's price skyrockets
articles.summary:
How much are you willing to pay to keep using your favorite app?
Maybe you’ve used it for years. Perhaps it performs a function so essential and specific that you couldn’t imagine what you’d do without it. But when the developer announces an extraordinary price hike, you’re forced to consider how much you really value that app.
Earlier this year, Evernote, a note-taking app, changed its subscription tiers, forcing some users to go from paying $130 per year to $250. The highest tier now costs more than 3.3 times as much as the most advanced tier did in 2023 and 10 times more than what Evernote charged for annual subscriptions from its 2008 launch until 2016.
That’s just one example of many longstanding consumer pieces of software that have seen dramatic price hikes in recent years. A lifetime pass to Plex, for example, was $75 in 2012. Today, it’s $250. Individual plans for Quicken, Robokiller, and Inkdrop have each doubled in price.
It’s easy to assume that the developers are miscalculating the value of their app or the loyalty of their users. But an unconventionally honest assessment regarding price hikes from Evernote owner Bending Spoons illustrates how owners of legacy software can apply pressure to loyal customers to extract additional revenue.
Evernote puts a fresh squeeze on old customers

The latest model generates the most photorealistic and interactive worlds yet, allowing users to type prompts mid-simulation to change the scene. The release of Genie 4 comes a couple of months after AI video startup Runway released its second world model, GWM Worlds 2, a playable model that responds dynamically to user inputs and includes audio generation. At the same time, the world model industry is beginning to consolidate. Fei-Fei Li’s World Labs is being acquired by AMD, Amazon is in talks to buy Decart, and Rivian just acquired Third Dimension to bring simulation capabilities in-house for self-driving testing.
Genie 4 is Google’s latest move to stay ahead in the crowded field.

Arquivos continuam no formato original e ganham colaboração em tempo real e histórico de versões.

Por depender de texto puro, ele é comum em documentação de software, repositórios de código e, mais recentemente, em arquivos utilizados por sistemas de inteligência artificial.
O Google Docs já oferecia algumas ferramentas para trabalhar com markdown. Desde 2024, era possível importar um arquivo .md, convertê-lo em um documento do Google e depois exportá-lo novamente em markdown. A diferença agora é que não há conversão.
Ao enviar um arquivo para o Drive e abri-lo no Docs, ele continua armazenado no formato original. O editor passa apenas a mostrar uma versão formatada do conteúdo, como um documento comum, e permite alterá-lo usando a interface tradicional do Docs.

articles.title: Qué es la terapia LED: la tendencia viral de cuidado de la piel que usa máscaras

Una tendencia que se ha hecho viral en redes sociales y por eso es importante conocerla al detalle para evitar problemas en la piel, saber cómo usarla y cuándo es el momento adecuado.
Qué es la terapia LED y cómo actúa sobre la piel
La terapia con luz LED utiliza longitudes de onda específicas para generar respuestas biológicas en los tejidos sin calor ni agresión, a diferencia de un láser. El mecanismo se denomina fotobiomodulación: una estimulación celular que no transforma la piel de forma inmediata, sino que acompaña procesos de recuperación e inflamación a lo largo de varias semanas de uso constante.
“La luz LED no calienta ni agrede la piel como puede hacerlo un láser. Actúa mediante fotobiomodulación, es decir, una estimulación biológica suave”, explicó la dermatóloga Natividad Cano a la revista Mujer Hoy.
El proceso ocurre a nivel mitocondrial. “Podemos imaginar las mitocondrias como pequeños motores dentro de las células” que transforman nutrientes y oxígeno en energía utilizable, describe Josh Adams, de Therabody. Cuando la luz roja o infrarroja incide sobre estas estructuras, ciertas enzimas la absorben y favorecen la liberación de óxido nítrico, lo que acelera la producción de energía celular disponible para tareas como s…

articles.title: Ford simplifies using your EV as a home battery with the $30K Fathom
articles.summary:
This morning, Ford revealed that buyers of the forthcoming Fathom—the company’s sub-$30,000 electric pickup truck due next year—will get more than just a truck. Until now, vehicle-to-home technology—like the setup Ford developed for the now-discontinued F-150 Lightning—takes DC power from the electric vehicle and runs it through an inverter built into the wallbox to turn it into AC the house can use. But with the Fathom, that inverter is built into the truck from the start. So every Fathom will be able to act as a backup battery for your home.
It’s typical: You wait a decade for a cheap electric truck, and then two come along almost at once. And they’re two radically different products from two radically different automakers that I think will reveal a few preferences from the EV-buying public. One is the Blank Slate, from a brand new startup offering a bare-bones two-door that capitalizes on features the Internet says it wants, like no onboard modem, no touchscreens, and no infotainment system.
The other is the result of one of Detroit’s big three taking a long, hard look at Chinese EVs and asking itself, “How do we make a car that cheap?” Although the Ford Fathom will cost $5,000 more than a Slate, that money does buy an extra pair of doors, modern conveniences like an infotainment system, CarPlay, electric windows, and a vast dealership network to service the car. That may be helpful given how many recalls Ford issues each year.

ChatGPT et Claude bannis en Suède à cause d’usages jugés problématiques, leur IA remplaçante est aussi américaine
Le gouvernement suédois interdit désormais à ses employés d’utiliser ChatGPT et Claude sur leurs ordinateurs professionnels, invoquant de sérieux risques pour la sécurité des données sensibles.
Depuis le lundi 26 octobre 2026, les agents du gouvernement suédois n’ont plus le droit d’accéder aux versions web de ChatGPT (OpenAI) et de Claude (Anthropic) depuis leurs postes de travail. Cette décision radicale fait suite à un audit interne mené plus tôt cette année au sein de l’Administration suédoise des transports. Les conclusions de cet examen ont mis en lumière de sérieuses dérives dans le partage d’informations sensibles et le traitement des réponses générées lors de la gestion des dossiers d’État.
La crainte du Shadow IT et la fuite d’informations hors des frontières européennes

Intel "Crescent Island" GPU Die Shows Up: 32 Xe3P Cores and 256 XMX Engines
Intel recently announced its D-series "Crescent Island" inference graphics cards, based on the Xe3P GPU microarchitecture, with the D270 being the highest-end SKU. The company's website has added a GPU bare die shot, revealing that the card is not the massive chip one might expect, but rather something seemingly smaller. The D270 GPU SKU features 32 Xe3P cores, 256 XMX engines, and 32 MB of unified L2 cache. The XMX engines have been redesigned from the four-deep systolic design of the regular Xe3 to 16-deep processing on the Xe3P. This card is intended for AI inferencing rather than training, so silicon requirements are secondary, and the card is rated for up to 480 GB of LPDDR5X.
Additional details include support for the FP4 data format alongside FP8, as well as large register files of 1 MB per core and an L1 cache of 512 KB per core. In total, there are 256 Vector engines and 256 of the new XMX engines, each divided into groups of eight per Xe3P core. Furthermore, the Xe3P lacks graphics processing elements for outputting imagery, as the silicon is designed purely for AI inference workloads that require long context and agentic tasks. Edge Sound Research Inc. today announced it has raised $2 million in new funding to build audio infrastructure that isolates useful sounds and combines them with other sensor data to help physical AI systems understand what’s happening in real time.
Stormbreaker Ventures led the round, bringing the company’s total funding to $9 million.
When the company first approached this problem, it looked at sports. When a basketball hits the court, fans are stomping in the stands and bass pounds through the arena’s speakers – all of this comes through microphones at the same time. For an artificial intelligence system trying to isolate the dribble, those overlapping sounds can make this difficult.
This challenge sits at the center of Edge Sound Research’s approach to machine perception: connecting audio with tracking and visual data to determine which sound belongs to which object.
“The issue in audio is it’s not object oriented; it’s channel oriented,” co-founder and Chief Executive Valtteri Salomaki told SiliconANGLE in an interview.
For broadcasters, making that connection means following a player’s sounds through a crowded arena. Edge is betting the same approach could help robots and other physical AI systems interpret the world around them — including activity their cameras cannot yet see.

Esto hace que el sentimiento que se tenga sea que las guarderías son auténticas bombas víricas, un ecosistema donde los patógenos saltan de niño a niño para terminar invariablemente en el hogar.

Ante este ciclo interminable de pediatras, antibióticos y malabarismos con las bajas laborales, la sabiduría popular suele ofrecer un consuelo: "Es bueno que lo pase ahora, así se inmuniza para cuando sea mayor". El efecto entrada. Cuando un niño entra en la guardería, el impacto en su salud a corto plazo es tan brusco que los investigadores lo tienen perfectamente cuantificado. Tokenmaxxing leaderboards miss the mark
Imagine a NASCAR team where leadership decides the winner is the car that burns the most fuel. The crew chief tunes every engine to run rich and wasteful. Drivers ride the gas and the brake at once. The telemetry shows record fuel consumption. The car finishes dead last.
For a stretch this year, wasteful consumption metrics drove AI measurement programs. Companies stood up internal leaderboards ranking employees by how many tokens they burned. A Meta employee built one, crowned the top "token legends," then quietly took it after the numbers leaked externally. By spring the trend had a name: tokenmaxxing.
By the start of summer the inevitable backlash arrived, with companies like Uber acknowledging they’d already spent their entire AI budget for the year in a matter of months.
CTO, ActivTrak.
More recently, the inevitable swing toward using the minimal number of AI tokens (tokenminning) leads to the same problem. If leadership defines winning as using the least amount of fuel, the winning car would never leave the starting line.
Burning or saving tokens should never be the end goal. The objective is shipping more products, at higher quality, with the same or fewer people. The job of a leader is to define the most strategic path toward the finish line, and based on that definition, build metrics that support it.

How to build sovereign AI infrastructure beyond data residency
As AI use expands globally, questions are emerging about where training data originates, who owns it, and how organizations keep sensitive information secure. Chief Business Officer at Supermicro.
Beyond where data is stored, sovereign AI is really a question of who controls an organization's or region's AI capabilities. In practice, this requires control over the entire infrastructure stack, both software and hardware, along with policies governing who can view data, manage infrastructure, and install software.
Because data protection laws and practices vary widely across geographies – even within Europe – the governance of data flows and processing pipelines must be understood and followed.
While sovereign AI is often discussed on a country-by-country basis, the same rules and procedures apply to enterprises. For them, questions of data location, ownership, and transmission are even more complex.
Location is only part of the story

articles.title: Crowdsourcing the corporate brain: Closing polanyi’s paradox on the frontline

Crowdsourcing the corporate brain: Closing polanyi’s paradox on the frontline
Frontline AI turns tacit worker knowledge into shared operational intelligence
Polymath Michael Polanyi famously noted, “We can know more than we can tell,” a paradox that’s now showing up and being solved on the warehouse and retail floor.
Frontline workers possess deep, tacit knowledge of how operations run, mastering practical workarounds, managing exceptions and localized efficiencies, and situational problem-solving. This knowledge never makes it into an official manual, yet real-life experience and multiple academic studies say that up to 85% of company knowledge is tacit.
VP for Automation, EMEA at Zebra Technologies.
Because this knowledge relies on muscle memory, experience, ad hoc conversations during lunch and notes, traditional top-down standard operating procedures (SOPs) inherently fail to capture it. Tacit knowledge enables employee competence, autonomy and job satisfaction, but can be unevenly distributed or lead to gatekeeping to the detriment of others. And when experienced or long-serving employees retire or move to a new company, that tacit knowledge is lost.
For years, businesses assumed their SOPs were rock-solid, but the rollout of frontline AI tools, such as AI knowledge agents trained on SOPs and other workforce onboarding and training materials, is bringing long-overlooked knowledge gaps and outdated guidelines to the surface.

articles.title: Steam Frame Gets Mainline Linux Support, Signalling SteamOS Alternatives for VR Gaming
articles.summary:
Tuesday, October 27th 2026
Steam Frame Gets Mainline Linux Support, Signalling SteamOS Alternatives for VR Gaming
The Valve Steam Frame has been supported in downstream SteamOS kernel builds since its launch in September, but a new set of patches submitted for inclusion in the mainline Linux kernel 7.4 will officially add support for the new VR headset in the mainline Linux kernel. The patches were submitted by Neil Armstrong on behalf of Valve Software and provide initial support for the Steam Frame. 
The patch notes specifically mention support for system reserved memory, regulators, GPIO keys PMIC functions, PMIC ADC channels, USB gadget, Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth, I2C and basic peripherals, and the built-in SD card slot. While support isn't yet feature-complete, it lays the groundwork for further kernel support down the line and should make it significantly easier for other distributions to support the Steam Frame without implementing a bunch of custom code and tools. This is also just one of many Linux 7.4 patches that will improve hardware support in the upcoming Linux kernel version.

AI’s value depends on data, governance and human judgement
One of AI’s biggest attractions is its ability to take time and effort out of everyday work. Tasks that would once have demanded hours of attention, such as turning meetings into notes or producing a first draft of a piece of content, can now be completed in minutes. These practical benefits help explain why AI has moved so quickly from experimentation into everyday business use.
Chief Strategy Officer at Qlik.
Yet, as AI becomes more established in the workplace, a more complicated picture is emerging. AI is changing where thinking happens. When a system can produce an answer almost instantly, the challenge shifts from creating the output to deciding what to do with it.
Employees are no longer spending as much time getting to a first answer, but they are spending more time checking whether the output is accurate, and critically, good enough to inform a decision. This creates a different kind of cognitive burden, moving from production to verification.
AI-generated outputs can appear remarkably polished and persuasive, even when they are based on incomplete information. An answer can sound convincing while overlooking a crucial piece of context or relying on incomplete information. And as AI becomes increasingly better at sounding confident, mistakes may look plausible enough to escape scrutiny and feed into business decisions without being challenged.

La edición nativa está diseñada para ejecutarse directamente en la nueva consola, sin depender de la retrocompatibilidad con Switch. Así, Mojang busca aprovechar las capacidades de Switch 2 y ofrecer una presentación visual mejorada.
Quiénes pueden actualizar gratis

articles.title: Critical Microsoft Authenticator flaw let malicious Android apps steal access to your precious accounts
articles.summary:
Critical Microsoft Authenticator flaw let malicious Android apps steal access to your precious accounts
Authenticator was granting session tokens left and right
- A critical Microsoft Authenticator flaw let rogue Android apps steal Microsoft session tokens without user interaction
- Attackers could impersonate trusted Microsoft apps and access emails, Teams data, calendars, and files
- Microsoft patched the bug and urges Android users to update Authenticator immediately
A critical vulnerability in the Microsoft Authenticator app for Android allowed malicious apps to obtain session tokens for pretty much any Microsoft app and hand them over to the attackers.
Unlike other Android malware, this one did not require extensive permissions, the victims did not need to approve the login process, and the attackers did not need to know their victim’s login credentials.
Found by researchers at Enclave, the vulnerability, now tracked as CVE_2026-80097, is fixed and Microsoft is urging all users to update their Authenticator app as soon as possible.
What is Authenticator and how was it abused?
Authenticator is Microsoft’s two-factor authentication (2FA) app. Besides users, it also allows other apps to authenticate, giving them session tokens that grant them access to the users’ Microsoft work account and associated data. In practice, it means that a legitimate app such as Microsoft Teams can log into a user’s work account through Authenticator.

articles.summary:
The Computer Emergency Response Team of Ukraine (CERT-UA) has issued an alert warning of unauthorized remote access to video surveillance systems manufactured by Dahua.
"Cases of compromising IP cameras and DVRs with access to the video stream, changing the device configuration and creating third-party accounts have been recorded," the State Special Communications Service of Ukraine (SSSCIP) said in an alert issued last week.
The primary initial access vector used in the attacks is via Easy4IP, a peer-to-peer (P2P) platform that allows users to remotely monitor homes or small businesses by connecting their Dahua IP cameras, NVRs, and DVRs via a smartphone app or web browser by scanning a QR code or entering the hardware Serial Number (SN).
The agency has warned that the serial numbers have a predictable structure containing a 10-character model prefix that's identical for all units of the same device family and a five-character hexadecimal counter that's incremented almost sequentially (e.g., 7K01F36PCA003E8).
This, in turn, allows attackers to guess them at scale through a brute-force attack and identify if they are connected to the cloud without hitting rate limits or lockouts. As a result, all devices with active P2P functionality are at risk even if they cannot be accessed directly via the internet.
"The assumption that the serial number is unknown to anyone is not a reason to consider the device secure," CERT-UA said.

articles.title: OpenAI Compaction Flaw Let Researchers Bypass Hidden Reasoning Protections
articles.summary:
OpenAI's compaction feature, which shrinks a long conversation to save space, could be turned into a way to copy a model's hidden reasoning out in plain text, security firm Xint has shown.
OpenAI's reasoning models work through a problem before answering, and the service normally returns only the raw reasoning as an encrypted item the user cannot read. The method got past the protections OpenAI added in August against this kind of reasoning theft. OpenAI confirmed the problem and fixed it on October 23, according to Xint.
Xint ran the technique against gpt-5.6-sol, one of OpenAI's reasoning models, using math and algorithm puzzles its researchers wrote themselves. The reasoning it pulled out came from those same requests, and Xint did not claim the method could reach another user's reasoning.
Xint says it cannot prove the copied text is word-for-word the model's real reasoning, because it never had the original to compare against. Two cheaper models each repeated the item and produced the same text, which rules out mistakes in the copying step but leaves open the possibility that compaction reworded the text.
Compaction is an OpenAI feature that uses a model to squeeze a long conversation into a smaller, encrypted item that carries the context forward.

Con ellos, un atacante podría acceder a servicios vinculados a Microsoft 365, como el correo, los archivos, el calendario, SharePoint y Teams.
El fallo, identificado como CVE-2026-80097, fue descubierto por investigadores de Enclave y comunicado a Microsoft. La compañía publicó una corrección para la aplicación. La vulnerabilidad no afecta a todos los usuarios de Microsoft Authenticator ni permite, por sí sola, atacar un teléfono a distancia: para que el escenario descrito fuera posible, la aplicación maliciosa tenía que estar instalada en el dispositivo.
Según el análisis de Enclave, una vez en el teléfono, esa aplicación podía solicitar un token haciéndose pasar por un servicio de Microsoft. Authenticator no comprobaba correctamente qué aplicación estaba realizando la petición y podía confiar en la identidad que esta declaraba. ASD is Australia's foreign signals intelligence and cyber security agency. Its offensive cyber operations need explicit approval from the Australian government and can disrupt cybercriminals overseas by disabling their infrastructure.
Amadey was sold to criminals as a service in 2018, according to ESET's analysis of Amadey. Each buyer runs its own control panel on its own servers.
Computers infected with Amadey check in with their buyer's command-and-control (C2) server and carry out its orders. Amadey's main job is to install more malware, such as the StealC infostealer. It can also steal credentials and give the buyer remote access to the machine.
The most common ways Amadey reached computers were fake software updates, cracked software installers, and other malware loaders.

Et si votre PlayStation 5 pouvait aussi faire tourner les jeux de votre bibliothèque Steam ? C’est la promesse de Playden, un launcher gratuit et open source qui fait fonctionner certains titres Windows directement sur la console. Une prouesse technique qui nécessite toutefois un jailbreak et quelques précautions.
Voir tourner des jeux PC sur une PlayStation 5 n’est plus seulement un fantasme de bidouilleur. Un développeur vient de mettre à disposition Playden sur GitHub, un client Steam non officiel et open source capable de télécharger les jeux vidéo de votre bibliothèque Steam et de les exécuter directement sur la console de Sony. Chaque titre dispose même de sa propre icône sur l’écran d’accueil comme s’il s’agissait d’un jeu PS5 classique.
Le projet, disponible gratuitement sur GitHub, est encore expérimental. Mais ses premiers résultats ont de quoi intriguer, notamment avec des titres aussi exigeants que Cyberpunk 2077.

Playden ne nécessite pas Windows ni SteamOS. Il s’appuie sur prospero-win, une adaptation de Wine qui permet d’exécuter des logiciels Windows sur le système de la PlayStation 5.
Le processeur AMD de la console utilisant la même architecture x86-64 que la plupart des PC, les jeux 64 bits n’ont pas besoin d’une émulation complète du processeur. La principale difficulté se situe plutôt du côté des bibliothèques système et de l'affichage.

articles.title: AI-Generated Fake Login Pages Are Making Account Takeovers Easier
articles.summary:
Fake login pages are nothing new, but generative AI is making them easier to build and more convincing. Attackers can recreate familiar login screens, impersonate trusted brands and tailor phishing attempts to specific employees or organizations.
Some fake login pages go beyond stealing passwords. They can also capture MFA codes or hijack authenticated sessions, allowing attackers to gain access to corporate accounts even when additional security measures are in place.
How AI is making fake login pages more convincing
Attackers have long used fake login pages to steal credentials, but generative AI makes it easier to create convincing replicas of legitimate authentication portals. From company logos and page layouts to login prompts, these fraudulent pages can closely resemble the websites employees regularly access.
AI also makes it easier to tailor phishing campaigns to specific organizations or employees. For example, attackers can create personalized IT notifications that direct employees to a fraudulent login page using the company's branding and familiar authentication prompts.
These attacks often rely on lookalike domains that closely resemble legitimate web addresses, with subtle spelling changes or additional characters. Combined with realistic login pages and targeted messaging, these tactics make phishing attempts harder to recognize.

An attacker who gained access to Keystone's website obtained the key that its hardware wallets use to prove they are genuine, the company said in a statement on October 26.
Someone with that key could build counterfeit devices that pass the online check owners use to verify a Keystone. A buyer who trusted a counterfeit could have their crypto stolen, but the incident did not involve owners' recovery phrases or wallet private keys.
Keystone will destroy 18,835 unsold devices that carry the key, and all new devices will get a new one.
Keystone found the unauthorized access on October 20, and its advice to owners depends on when a device arrived. For a device received after that date with the old key, the company said: "Even if such a device passes authentication, we cannot completely rule out the possibility that it is counterfeit."
Owners of such a device should contact Keystone support and use it only after the company confirms it is genuine.
A device delivered before October 20 that passes the check can be considered genuine and used normally, according to Keystone. The company has not said when the attacker first got in.
The attacker exploited a vulnerability in a third-party data monitoring tool used by Keystone's website to escalate privileges, according to the company. That let the attacker obtain customer data and the key.
Keystone blocked the attacker's access on October 20 and has since fixed the vulnerability. It has not said where the key was stored.

Il a aussi relevé, dans la requête, différents marqueurs typographiques qu’il attribue à l’intelligence artificielle générative.
Ni urgence ni doute sérieux pour le tribunal administratif
L'affaire a démarré avec un refus d'admission en première année de master de psychologie, opposé par l'université Rennes 2 à Delphine*, une étudiante qui ne voulait pas en rester là. articles.summary:
Microsoft has fixed a flaw in its Authenticator app for Android that let a malicious app with no permissions pose as a trusted Microsoft app, such as Teams, and collect sign-in tokens for a victim's work account.
Microsoft tracks the flaw as CVE-2026-80097 and fixed it in Authenticator for Android version 6.2606.4246, so anyone using the app should update.
In the researchers' tests, the tokens gave full access to the account's email, files, and calendar. Microsoft says exploitation also needs the victim to complete a sign-in step in Authenticator, and that the flaw has not been used in attacks.
The research comes from Ofek Levin, working through a fellowship program at the security firm Enclave, which published the technical details on October 23, 2026. Microsoft assigned the CVE on September 8 and rated it 8.6 on the CVSS scale, which it labels "Important."
On Android, Authenticator does more than show six-digit codes. It also acts as a broker: when Teams, Outlook, or another Microsoft app needs to sign a user in, it asks Authenticator, and Authenticator hands back a token, a digital pass that proves the user is logged in. Because the broker controls access to the entire account, it should be careful about which app it grants a token to.

T-Mobile, Nokia, and Nvidia say they have completed the world's first AI-RAN (Artificial Intelligence - Radio Access Network) call, routed through a commercial cell site in Bellevue, Washington.
The call ran over T-Mobile's live production network using a Nokia Massive MIMO radio, Nokia's 5G anyRAN software and servers built on Nvidia's Aerial RAN Computer (ARC) platform.
This wasn't a lab rig with test handsets, either, but a real-world setup that held; according to Nvidia's announcement, the site connected to T-Mobile's existing 5G Standalone core and a commercial smartphone.
What is an AI-RAN and why is it relevant now?
The radio access network (RAN) is the part of a mobile network your phone actually talks to: the antennas, radios, and baseband computers that process signals at each cell site. That processing has traditionally run on custom chips.

articles.title: GoAhead TLS Flaws Allow Revoked Client Certificates and Enable Session Decryption
articles.summary:
The GoAhead embedded web server loaded a certificate revocation list into its default TLS backend but never turned revocation checking on, so a revoked client certificate could still pass login on affected setups.
The flaw is in builds that use the OpenSSL backend with mutual-TLS, where the server checks a client certificate and vice versa, and a revocation list is configured to block revoked certificates.
That is a setup an operator turns on deliberately; a default build does not. GoAhead 6.1.1, released to device makers on August 2, 2026, and publicly published on October 12, fixes it.
GoAhead is a small web server that device makers build into firmware to run management pages on routers, printers, gateways and industrial controllers. Its maker, EmbedThis, says it runs in hundreds of millions of devices.
The flaw was found by Sébastien Féry of FoxIO, who described it and two other TLS problems in a write-up on October 26.
On an affected build, the server loads the revocation list file at startup and reports no error, so an operator who configured it has every reason to think revocation is working. It is not. A client whose certificate was revoked, for example a stolen or retired device, completes the handshake as if the certificate were still valid and gets whatever access that identity allows.
In FoxIO's test against GoAhead 6.1.0 with OpenSSL 3.6.2, a revoked certificate was accepted with issuer checking switched on.
